'''Bring Me the Horizon''' are <!-- Per WP:ENGVAR, British English treats collective nouns plural. Please don't change this to "is" without discussion on the talk page (click "talk" tab at top of page). --> a British [[Rock music|rock]] band, formed in [[Sheffield]], England in 2004. The group currently consists of lead vocalist [[Oli Sykes]], drummer [[Matt Nicholls]], guitarist [[Lee Malia]] and bassist [[Matt Kean (musician)|Matt Kean]]. They are signed to [[RCA Records]] globally and [[Columbia Records]] exclusively in the United States.

The band released their debut album ''[[Count Your Blessings (Bring Me the Horizon album)|Count Your Blessings]]'' in 2006. The album featured a deathcore sound that the band would move away from starting with their second album ''[[Suicide Season]]'' (2008). The album was considered a creative, critical and commercial turning point for the band. Bring Me the Horizon released their third album, ''[[There Is a Hell Believe Me I've Seen It. There Is a Heaven Let's Keep It a Secret.]]'', in 2010, propelling them to greater international fame, whilst incorporating influences from [[classical music]], [[electronica]] and [[pop music|pop]]. Their major label debut, ''[[Sempiternal (album)|Sempiternal]]'', (2013) achieved Gold certification in Australia (35,000) and Silver in the United Kingdom (60,000). ''[[That's the Spirit]]'' (2015) debuted at number two in the [[UK Albums Chart]] and the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Liv|url=http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/stereophonics-bag-sixth-number-1-album-with-keep-the-village-alive-thank-you-all-__10769/|title=Stereophonics bag sixth Number 1 album: "Thank you all"|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918161819/http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/stereophonics-bag-sixth-number-1-album-with-keep-the-village-alive-thank-you-all-__10769/|archive-date=18 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizons-thats-the-spirit-lands-at-no-2-on-the-billboard-200-chart/|title=Bring Me the Horizon's 'That's The Spirit' Lands At No. 2 On The Billboard 200 Chart|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=1 April 2017|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630211854/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizons-thats-the-spirit-lands-at-no-2-on-the-billboard-200-chart/|archive-date=30 June 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Their sixth studio album ''[[Amo (Bring Me the Horizon album)|Amo]]'' (2019) became their first UK chart-topper. In the same year, the band also released ''[[Music to Listen To...]]'' (2019). ''[[Post Human: Survival Horror]]'' followed in 2020, the first in a planned series of four projects under the ''Post Human'' name, with the second installment, ''[[Post Human: Nex Gen]]'', released as their seventh studio album in May 2024. The band have also released two extended plays and two live albums. They have received [[List of Kerrang! Award winners|seven]] [[Kerrang! Awards|''Kerrang!'' Awards]], including two for Best British Band and one for Best Live Band, a [[Brit Award for British Rock/Alternative Act|BRIT Award for Best Rock/Alternative Act]] and have been nominated for two [[Grammy Award]]s. The band has sold over 5 million records worldwide, and have [[List of artists by number of UK Rock & Metal Singles Chart number ones|topped the UK Rock & Metal Singles Chart]] with songs such as "[[Throne (song)|Throne]]", "[[Drown (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Drown]]", "[[Mantra (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Mantra]]", "[[Parasite Eve (song)|Parasite Eve]]", "[[Teardrops (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Teardrops]]", and "[[Kool-Aid (song)|Kool-Aid]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sonymusic.co.uk/artist/bring-me-the-horizon/|title=Bring Me The Horizon|work=[[Sony Music]]|access-date=11 May 2022|archive-date=26 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220626074438/https://www.sonymusic.co.uk/artist/bring-me-the-horizon/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The style of their early work, including their debut album ''Count Your Blessings'', has been described primarily as [[deathcore]], but over the course of several albums, the band has shifted its style and moved in a more melodically-orientated direction by combining their approach to metalcore with elements of [[electronica]], [[pop music|pop]] and [[Hip hop music|hip hop]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Lukas|last=Wojcicki|url=https://exclaim.ca/music/article/bring_me_the_horizon-amo|title=Bring Me the Horizon amo|work=[[Exclaim!]]|date=24 January 2019|access-date=24 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929134801/http://exclaim.ca/music/article/bring_me_the_horizon-amo|archive-date=29 September 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="loudwire">{{cite web|url=http://loudwire.com/why-did-bring-me-the-horizon-go-pop/|title=Why Did Bring Me the Horizon Go Pop?|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=25 January 2019|access-date=25 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102005628/https://loudwire.com/why-did-bring-me-the-horizon-go-pop/|archive-date=2 November 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

==History==

===Formation and early releases (2002–2006)===
<!-- The use of 2002 instead of 2004 in the title is to point out any information about the members prior to the formation of the band. Example article: The Clash -->
{{Main|This Is What the Edge of Your Seat Was Made For}}
Bring Me the Horizon's founding members came from diverse musical backgrounds within metal and rock. [[Matt Nicholls]] and [[Oliver Sykes]] had a common interest in American [[metalcore]] such as [[Norma Jean (band)|Norma Jean]] and [[Skycamefalling]], and used to attend local [[hardcore punk]] shows. They later met [[Lee Malia]], who spoke with them about [[thrash metal]] and [[melodic death metal]] bands like [[Metallica]] and [[At the Gates]]; Malia had also been part of a Metallica tribute band before meeting the pair.{{sfn|Patterson|2011|p=45}} Bring Me the Horizon officially formed in March 2004, when the members were aged 15 to 17.{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=50}} Curtis Ward, who also lived in the [[Rotherham]] area, joined Sykes, Nicholls and Malia on drums. Bassist [[Matt Kean (musician)|Matt Kean]], who was in other local bands, completed the line-up.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} Their name is taken from a line of dialogue spoken by [[Captain Jack Sparrow]] in the 2003 film ''[[Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl]]'', in which Sparrow says: "Now, bring me that horizon."<ref name="spin nov2010">{{cite magazine|first=David|last=Marchese|url=https://www.spin.com/2010/11/why-theyre-called-bring-me-horizon/|title=Why They're Called... Bring Me The Horizon|magazine=[[Spin (magazine)|Spin]]|date=22 November 2010|access-date=29 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110829054955/https://www.spin.com/2010/11/why-theyre-called-bring-me-horizon/|archive-date=29 August 2011|url-status=live}}</ref>

In the months following their formation, Bring Me the Horizon created a demo album titled ''Bedroom Sessions''. They followed this by releasing their first [[extended play|EP]], ''[[This Is What the Edge of Your Seat Was Made For]]'', in September 2004 through local UK label Thirty Days of Night Records.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} Bring Me the Horizon were the label's first signing.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://drownedinsound.com/directory/labels/Thirty_Days_Of_Night_Records|title=Thirty Days Of Night Records|work=[[Drowned in Sound]]|access-date=6 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004214223/http://drownedinsound.com/directory/labels/Thirty_Days_Of_Night_Records|archive-date=4 October 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> It was recorded at Pristine Studios in Nottingham over the course of two weekends, with drums and bass laid down over the first weekend, and guitars and vocals completed a week later.<ref name="rockfreaks 1">{{cite web|first=Aleksi|last=Pertola|url=http://www.rockfreaks.net/interviews/225|title=Bring Me the Horizon Bassist Discusses Guitarist's Departure|work=RockFreaks|date=11 February 2011|access-date=2 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406201617/http://www.rockfreaks.net/interviews/225|archive-date=6 April 2012|url-status=live}}</ref>

UK label [[Visible Noise]] noticed the band after the release of their EP,{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} and signed them for a four-album deal, in addition to re-releasing the EP in January 2005.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} The re-release gained the band significant attention, eventually peaking at No. 41 on the UK album charts.<ref name="zobbel.de">{{cite web|url=http://www.zobbel.de/cluk/CLUK_B.HTM|title=Chart Log UK Darren B – David Byrne|access-date=30 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091226170502/http://www.zobbel.de/cluk/CLUK_B.HTM|archive-date=26 December 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> The band was later awarded Best British Newcomer at the [[Kerrang! Awards#2006|2006 Kerrang! Awards]] ceremony.<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Brown|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2006/aug/25/arts.media|title=Lostprophets on their metal as they top the Kerrang! awards|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=25 August 2006|access-date=6 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005091243/http://www.theguardian.com/uk/2006/aug/25/arts.media|archive-date=5 October 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

The band's first tour was supporting [[The Red Chord]] across the United Kingdom.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} As with other early tours, they were able to get this slot by tricking venue promoters. Kean and Oliver's mother Carol Sykes were the de facto managers of the band at this time, a role they continued to occupy until 2008.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} For The Red Chord support, Kean emailed promoters and pretended they were opening on all the dates, when they were supposed to play only at their local show. This led them to being booked for the whole tour. In another case, Sykes created an e-mail account in the name of [[Johnny Truant]] vocalist Oliver Mitchell, which he used to contact a promoter requesting Bring Me the Horizon on their tour.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}} Alcohol consumption fuelled their live performances in their early history when the band would get so drunk they vomited on stage and damaged their equipment.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=65}}

===''Count Your Blessings'' (2006–2007)===
{{Main|Count Your Blessings (Bring Me the Horizon album)|l1=Count Your Blessings}}
[[File:Bring-Me-The-Horizon.jpg|thumb|right|Bring Me the Horizon in Vienna]]
The band released their debut album ''[[Count Your Blessings (Bring Me the Horizon album)|Count Your Blessings]]'' in October 2006 in the United Kingdom<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thenewfury.com/this-day-music-history-bring-horizon-debut-full-length-album-count-your-blessings/|title=This Day In Music History: October 30th, 2006 – Bring Me The Horizon releases debut album, 'Count Your Blessings'|work=The New Fury|date=30 October 2006|access-date=1 June 2024}}</ref> and in August 2007 in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-count-your-blessings-to-receive-u-s-release-in-august/|title=Bring Me The Horizon: 'Count Your Blessings' To Receive U.S. Release In August|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=22 May 2007|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822213857/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-count-your-blessings-to-receive-u-s-release-in-august/|archive-date=22 August 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> They rented a house in the country to write songs, but easily became distracted. They then recorded the album in inner-city Birmingham, a process which was infamous for their excessive and dangerous drinking. During this period drummer Nicholls summarised it saying "we were out every night, just being regular 18-year-olds".{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=67}} Critics panned the album adding to the strongly polarised responses the band were already seeing from the public.{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=50}}

They supported ''Count Your Blessings'' by going on a lengthy headline tour of the UK in November,<ref name="Dis-party music">{{cite web|first=Raziq|last=Rauf|url=http://drownedinsound.com/in_depth/1263353|title=Bring Me The Horizon: "It's just party music"|work=[[Drowned In Sound]]|date=6 November 2006|access-date=7 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014072647/http://drownedinsound.com/in_depth/1263353|archive-date=14 October 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> and immediately followed this joining [[Lostprophets]] and [[The Blackout (band)|The Blackout]] on a UK tour<ref>{{cite web|first=Caroline|last=Jones|url=http://www.gigwise.com/article.php?contentid=25949|title=Saturday 09/12/06 Lostprophets, Bring Me The Horizon, The Blackout @ Hammersmith Apollo, London|work=[[Gigwise]]|date=13 December 2006|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110609025336/http://www.gigwise.com/article.php?contentid=25949|archive-date=9 June 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> through late November and December 2006.

In January 2007, Bring Me the Horizon were able to set their sights beyond the UK, when they replaced [[Bury Your Dead]] on [[Killswitch Engage]]'s European headline tour. The slot became available after Bury Your Dead were forced to withdraw by the departure from the band of their vocalist, Mat Bruso.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-replaces-bury-your-dead-on-killswitch-engage-s-european-tour|title=Bring Me the Horizon Replaces Bury Your Dead On Killswitch Engage's European Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=7 January 2007|access-date=29 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230226090309/https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-replaces-bury-your-dead-on-killswitch-engage-s-european-tour|archive-date=26 February 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> Bring Me the Horizon's presence on the tour was poorly received by fans of Killswitch Engage, with concert attendees regularly [[Bottling (concert abuse)|throwing bottles]] at the band before they even started playing their set.{{sfn|Ritchie|2012|p=54}}

===''Suicide Season'' and Ward's departure (2008–2009)===
{{Main|Suicide Season}}
Bring Me the Horizon recorded their second studio album, ''[[Suicide Season]]'', in Sweden with producer [[Fredrik Nordström]]. He was unimpressed with their first album and was initially absent from the recording sessions unless he needed to be there. Nordström later heard the new sound they were experimenting with during a recording session and became very involved in the record.{{sfn|Ritchie|2012|p=56}} It was promoted virally in the weeks before its release with the promotional tag line "September is Suicide Season."<ref name="September is Suicide Season">{{cite web|url=http://news.mibba.com/Music/1232/September-Is-Suicide-Season|title=September Is 'Suicide Season'|work=mibba|date=28 July 2008|access-date=18 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111007050808/http://news.mibba.com/Music/1232/September-Is-Suicide-Season|archive-date=7 October 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> To promote ''Suicide Season'' the band embarked on their first headline tour of the United States,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.epitaph.com/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-launch-us-tour|title=Bring Me the Horizon Launch U.S. Tour|work=[[Epitaph Records]]|date=29 October 2008|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412222836/https://www.epitaph.com/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-launch-us-tour|archive-date=12 April 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> as well as appearing at the 2008 [[Warped Tour]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.altpress.com/vans_warped_tour_2008_look_back/|title=A look back at Warped Tour 2008|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=28 February 2018|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125012728/https://www.altpress.com/vans_warped_tour_2008_look_back/|archive-date=25 November 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2008, Bring Me the Horizon was the main supporting band on [[I Killed the Prom Queen]]'s farewell Australian tour with [[The Ghost Inside (band)|The Ghost Inside]] and [[The Red Shore]].<ref name="iktpq tour 2008">{{cite web|url=http://www.fasterlouder.com.au/news/local/12509/I-Killed-The-Prom-Queen-farewell-tour|title=I Killed The Prom Queen farewell tour|work=Faster Louder|date=3 March 2008|access-date=18 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110315001125/http://www.fasterlouder.com.au/news/local/12509/I-Killed-The-Prom-Queen-farewell-tour|archive-date=15 March 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

''Suicide Season'' was released on 18 September 2008 in the United States on [[Epitaph Records|Epitaph]] and on 29 September in Europe through Visible Noise. In 2009, Bring Me the Horizon attended the [[Kerrang! Tour#Kerrang! Tour 2009|2009 Kerrang! Tour]] alongside [[Black Tide]], [[Dir En Grey]], [[In Case of Fire]] and [[Mindless Self Indulgence]].<ref name="kerrangtour2010">{{cite magazine|author=Dan|url=http://www.kerrang.com/blog/2008/10/kerrang_relentless_energy_drin.html|title=Kerrang! Relentless Energy Drink Tour 2009 is go!|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=22 October 2008|access-date=29 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713144649/http://www.kerrang.com/blog/2008/10/kerrang_relentless_energy_drin.html|archive-date=13 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> They also joined [[Thursday (band)|Thursday]], [[Cancer Bats]], [[Four Year Strong]] and [[Pierce the Veil]] on the North American leg of the 2009 [[Taste of Chaos]] tour from February to April{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=67}} after the tour's organizer [[Kevin Lyman]] offered them the slot. The band were initially hesitant to join this tour, but were convinced after Lyman offered them a bus and $500 of fuel for the tour.<ref name="RS-classic BFMV"/>

[[File:Jona bmth 091709.jpg|thumb|right|[[Jona Weinhofen]] joined the band in 2009 after leaving [[Bleeding Through]].|255x255px]]
During the Taste of Chaos tour in March of that year, guitarist Curtis Ward left the band.<ref name="curtis quit the band">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.idiomag.com/peek/73480/bring_me_the_horizon|title=Bring Me the Horizon Bassist Discusses Guitarist's Departure|magazine=[[idiomag]]|date=1 April 2009|access-date=1 April 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090506055453/http://www.idiomag.com/peek/73480/bring_me_the_horizon|archive-date=6 May 2009|url-status=live}}</ref> His relationship with the band had deteriorated as his stage performances were poor. He was abusive to audiences during the Taste of Chaos tour,{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=67}} and had contributed little to the writing of ''Suicide Season''.<ref name="rockfreaks 1"/> Another reason for his departure was the worsening [[tinnitus]] in his one functioning ear. Ward was born deaf in one ear and admitted playing in the band worsened the ringing in his other ear to such a degree that he was unable to sleep at night.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/bringmethehorizon|title=Bring Me The Horizon|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=13 July 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140305062855/http://www.altpress.com/features/entry/bringmethehorizon|archive-date=5 March 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ward offered to perform the rest of the tour dates, which the band rejected and instead asked their guitar technician, Dean Rowbotham, to substitute for him for the remaining performances.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=67}} Lee Malia noted that Ward's departure helped improve everyone's mood as he had been very negative.{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=67}} Within a week of the tour finishing, Sykes began talking to [[Jona Weinhofen]], at the time the guitarist of [[Bleeding Through]]. The band knew of him from his work with his former band I Killed the Prom Queen,{{sfn|Patashnik|2012|p=67}} and he was asked to join them.<ref name="Kerrang 1269">{{cite magazine|date= 11 July 2009|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|issue= 1269|title=Kerrang Bauer Consumer Media|publisher= [[Bauer Consumer Media]]|editor=Nichola Browne|location= London, United Kingdom|issn=0262-6624}}</ref> Ward has since worked on the TV show [[Top Gear (2002 TV Series)|Top Gear]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9IZwqKanwWQ|title=Oliver Sykes And Lee &#124; Funny Interview [BMTH&#93; Bring Me The Horizon|publisher=[[YouTube]]|date=10 June 2012|access-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307205128/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9IZwqKanwWQ|archive-date=7 March 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> and has occasionally performed on stage with Bring Me The Horizon, playing "Pray For Plagues", most notably at [[Wembley Arena]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WBEJSX6_DLs|title=Bring Me The Horizon – Live At Wembley Full Concert HD|publisher=[[YouTube]]|date=4 November 2015|access-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160519011814/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WBEJSX6_DLs&gl=US&hl=en|archive-date=19 May 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2016, it was announced that Ward had joined the band Counting Days.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/counting-days-curtis-ward-bring-me-the-horizon|title=Counting Days recruit ex Bring Me The Horizon man Curtis Ward|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=15 April 2016|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240405205426/https://www.loudersound.com/news/counting-days-curtis-ward-bring-me-the-horizon|archive-date=5 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

In November 2009, Bring Me the Horizon released a remixed version of ''Suicide Season'', titled ''[[Suicide Season: Cut Up!]]'' Musicians and producers featured on the album include: [[Ben Weinman]], [[Skrillex]], [[L'Amour La Morgue]], [[Utah Saints]] and [[Shawn Crahan]].<ref name="rocksound.tv">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-remix-suicide-season|title=Bring Me The Horizon Remix Suicide Season|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=27 August 2009|access-date=1 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100418070428/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-remix-suicide-season|archive-date=18 April 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Andrew|last=Kelham|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/reviews/article/bring-me-the-horizon-suicide-season-cut-up|title=Bring Me The Horizon – Suicide Season – Cut Up|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=2 November 2009|access-date=28 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513020548/http://www.rocksound.tv/reviews/article/bring-me-the-horizon-suicide-season-cut-up|archive-date=13 May 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===''There Is a Hell...'' (2010–2011)===
{{Main|There Is a Hell Believe Me I've Seen It. There Is a Heaven Let's Keep It a Secret.}}
The band's third album, and first with their new rhythm guitarist [[Jona Weinhofen]], titled ''[[There Is a Hell Believe Me I've Seen It. There Is a Heaven Let's Keep It a Secret.]]'', was released on 4 October 2010 and debuted at number 17 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] in the United States,<ref>{{cite magazine|title=There Is a Hell, Believe Me I've Seen It, There is a Heaven, Let's Keep It a Secret – Bring Me the Horizon|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/bring-me-the-horizon/chart-history/|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=16 October 2010|archive-date=21 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211121093755/https://www.billboard.com/artist/bring-me-the-horizon/chart-history/|url-status=live}}</ref> number 13 on the [[UK Album Chart]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theofficialcharts.com/artist/_/bring%20me%20the%20horizon/|title=Official Charts – Album Charts|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=29 June 2011}}</ref> and number one on the [[Australian Albums Chart]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_album.asp?chart=1G50|title=ARIA Top 50 Albums Chart|work=[[Australian Recording Industry Association]]|access-date=18 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120502043844/http://ariacharts.com.au/pages/charts_display_album.asp?chart=1G50|archive-date=2 May 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> the [[UK Rock Chart]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theofficialcharts.com/rock-charts/|title=Official Charts – Rock Charts|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=16 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101012191521/http://www.theofficialcharts.com/rock-charts/|archive-date=12 October 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the [[UK Indie Chart]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theofficialcharts.com/alternative-charts/|title=Official Charts – Alternative Charts|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=16 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101010123622/http://www.theofficialcharts.com/alternative-charts/|archive-date=10 October 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> Despite reaching number one in Australia, the album's sales were the lowest for a number one album in the history of the [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA) charts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pedestrian.tv/music/news/71964-dollars-buys-you-the-number-1-album-in-austr/25402.htm|title=71,964 Dollars Buys You The Number 1 Album in Australia|date=19 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111006150718/http://www.pedestrian.tv/music/news/71964-dollars-buys-you-the-number-1-album-in-austr/25402.htm|archive-date=6 October 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Matt Nicholls describes the lyrical themes of ''There Is a Hell''... as being "repercussions of everything we were singing about on our last CD [Suicide Season]," calling the music and lyrics a lot moodier and darker.<ref name="rockfreaks 1"/> Five singles  were released from the album including: "[[It Never Ends]]", "Anthem", "[[Blessed with a Curse]]", "Visions", and "Alligator Blood", with music videos produced for each of the songs. The band embarked on a headline tour in intimate venues across the United Kingdom with support from Cancer Bats and Tek-One.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bmthcbuktour|title=Bring Me The Horizon And Cancer Bats For Tiny Venue UK Tour|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=13 April 2010|access-date=24 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110105105637/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bmthcbuktour|archive-date=5 January 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> In December 2010, Bring Me the Horizon joined [[Bullet for My Valentine]] as the main support band, alongside [[Atreyu (band)|Atreyu]], on a short five-date arena tour around the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-support-bullet-for-my-valentine-on-arena-tour|title=Bring Me The Horizon Support Bullet For My Valentine On Arena Tour|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=31 July 2010|access-date=2 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100803013323/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-support-bullet-for-my-valentine-on-arena-tour|archive-date=3 August 2010|url-status=live}}</ref> To cope with high demand, [[Live Nation]] released extra standing tickets for all dates.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.glasswerk.co.uk/news/national/9580/Bring+Me+The+Horizon+To+Support+Bullet+For+My+Valentine|title=News \ Bring Me The Horizon To Support Bullet For My Valentine|publisher=Glasswerk National|date=2 August 2010|access-date=2 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004115354/http://www.glasswerk.co.uk/news/national/9580/Bring%2BMe%2BThe%2BHorizon%2BTo%2BSupport%2BBullet%2BFor%2BMy%2BValentine|archive-date=4 October 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:Bmth.jpg|thumb|left|Bring Me the Horizon in 2011]]
In April 2011, Bring Me the Horizon embarked on a European tour, starting in the United Kingdom. They toured with [[Parkway Drive]], [[Architects (British band)|Architects]], and [[The Devil Wears Prada (band)|The Devil Wears Prada]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Aaron|last=Fowler|url=https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_announce_spring_2011_uk_tour_with_the_devil_wears_prad/|title=Bring Me The Horizon announce Spring 2011 UK tour with The Devil Wears Prada and Parkway Drive|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=1 December 2010|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105164715/https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_announce_spring_2011_uk_tour_with_the_devil_wears_prad/|archive-date=5 November 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 April, Nicholls broke his arm whilst playing football with members of Bring Me the Horizon, Parkway Drive and Architects. Instead of cancelling the tour, Architects' drummer Dan Searle filled in as drummer, but this meant that Bring Me the Horizon's setlist was halved in length.<ref name="mattbreaks arm">{{cite web|first=Katie|last=Parsons|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-59-1295300|title=Bring Me The Horizon drummer Matt Nicholls breaks arm during UK tour|work=[[NME]]|date=28 April 2008|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230427155232/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-59-1295300|archive-date=27 April 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The tour was extended with a North American leg from 13 August to 4 October, retaining Parkway Drive and Architects and adding [[Deez Nuts (band)|Deez Nuts]] to the line up.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Ableson|url=http://www.alterthepress.com/2011/07/bring-me-horizon-us-tour-w-parkway.html|title=Alter the Press!: Bring Me The Horizon US Tour w/ Parkway Drive|work=Alter The Press!|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004235253/http://www.alterthepress.com/2011/07/bring-me-horizon-us-tour-w-parkway.html|archive-date=4 October 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> On 23 August they released the fourth music video and single, "Visions",<ref>{{cite magazine|first=James|last=Gill|url=http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/top-posts/new-bring-me-the-horizon-video-online/|title=Metal Hammer – Blog Archive – New Bring Me The Horizon Video Online|magazine=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=24 August 2011|access-date=24 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120925072443/http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/top-posts/new-bring-me-the-horizon-video-online/|archive-date=25 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> and on 31 October the music video for the song "Alligator Blood" was released.<ref>{{cite web|first=Liz|last=Ramanand|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-alligator-blood-video/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Let Loose Video for 'Alligator Blood'|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=31 October 2011|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418101249/https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-alligator-blood-video/|archive-date=18 April 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2011, [[Machine Head (band)|Machine Head]] completed an arena tour across Europe with Bring Me the Horizon as the main support band along with [[DevilDriver]] and [[Darkest Hour (band)|Darkest Hour]]. Oliver Sykes said these would be the last European dates before they began writing and the recording their fourth album.<ref name="NME 2">{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Goodwyn|url=https://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/57470|title=Bring Me The Horizon: 'Machine Head tour will be our last UK dates for a while'|work=[[NME]]|date=22 June 2011|access-date=17 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110626144026/http://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/57470|archive-date=26 June 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> 2011 ended with an announcement by the band on 29 December of a new extended play titled ''[[The Chill Out Sessions]]'', a collaborative effort with British DJ Draper.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.alterthepress.com/2011/12/bring-me-horizon-to-release-remix-album.html|title=Bring Me The Horizon To Release Remix Album "The Chill Out Sessions"|access-date=4 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120114080431/http://www.alterthepress.com/2011/12/bring-me-horizon-to-release-remix-album.html|archive-date=14 January 2012|url-status=live}} Alter The Press! 30 December 2011. Retrieved 6 January 2012.</ref> Draper first released an "officially sanctioned" remix of the song "Blessed with a Curse" in May 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theprp.com/2011/05/13/news/drapers-remix-of-bring-me-the-horizons-blessed-with-a-curse-available-for-streaming/|title=Draper's Remix Of Bring Me The Horizon's "Blessed With A Curse" Available For Streaming|work=The PRP|date=13 May 2011|access-date=6 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130328050031/http://www.theprp.com/2011/05/13/news/drapers-remix-of-bring-me-the-horizons-blessed-with-a-curse-available-for-streaming/|archive-date=28 March 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> The EP was originally supposed to be released in time for New Year's Day, and made available for download and purchase though Bring Me the Horizon's website, but the EP's release was cancelled due to the band's "current management and label situation".<ref>{{cite news |title=Bring Me The Horizon remix "The Chill Out Sessions" release cancelled |url=http://rawtuneage.indiestar.tv/2011/12/bring-me-horizon-collaborates-with.html |access-date=6 January 2012 |publisher=Raw Tuneage |date=29 December 2011 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111150412/http://rawtuneage.indiestar.tv/2011/12/bring-me-horizon-collaborates-with.html |archive-date=11 January 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Redrup|url=http://www.deadpress.co.uk/9723/news-bring-me-the-horizon-pull-the-chill-out-sessions-remix-album/|title=News: Bring Me The Horizon pull 'The Chill Out Sessions' remix album!|work=Dead Press|date=29 December 2011|access-date=6 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322021137/http://www.deadpress.co.uk/9723/news-bring-me-the-horizon-pull-the-chill-out-sessions-remix-album/|archive-date=22 March 2012|url-status=live}}</ref>

===''Sempiternal'' and Weinhofen's departure (2012–2014)===
{{Main|Sempiternal (album)|l1=Sempiternal}}
[[File:2016 RiP Bring Me the Horizon - Jordan Fish - by 2eight - 8SC6495.jpg|thumb|left|[[Jordan Fish]] joined the band in 2012, after originally being asked to contribute as a session member.]]
After an intense touring schedule, Bring Me the Horizon finally completed their third album's promotion at the end of 2011. They returned to the UK for an extended break and eventually starting work on their next album.<ref name="Blabbermouth-4th album start">{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=168892|title = Bring Me the Horizon To Begin Writing New Album Next Month|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=27 January 2012|access-date=23 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102235007/http://blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=168892|archive-date=2 November 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Much like their previous two albums, they wrote their fourth album in seclusion and isolation to stay focused. This time, they retreated to a house in the [[Lake District]]. In July, the band started to publish images of themselves recording at a 'Top Secret Studio Location,'<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Mike|last=Hohnen|url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-me-the-horizon-begin-work-on-new-album-at-top-secret-studio-location/|title=Bring Me The Horizon Begin Work On New Album At 'Top Secret Studio Location'|magazine=[[Music Feeds]]|date=19 July 2012|access-date=28 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720222008/http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-me-the-horizon-begin-work-on-new-album-at-top-secret-studio-location/|archive-date=20 July 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> and revealed they were working with producer [[Terry Date]] for the recording and production of the album.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-enter-the-studio-confirm-producer-for-album-4|title=Bring Me The Horizon Enter The Studio, Confirm Producer For Album #4|magazine=[[Rocksound]]|date=19 September 2012|access-date=27 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120923034644/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-enter-the-studio-confirm-producer-for-album-4|archive-date=23 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 30 July, the band announced they had left their label and signed with [[RCA Records|RCA]], who would release their fourth album in 2013.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-announce-new-record-label|title=Bring Me The Horizon Announce New Record Label|magazine=[[Rocksound]]|date=30 July 2012|access-date=30 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120731073905/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/article/bring-me-the-horizon-announce-new-record-label|archive-date=31 July 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band played only three shows in all of 2012: [[Warped Tour 2012#Europe|Warped Tour 2012]] on 10 November at the [[Alexandra Palace]] in London, which they headlined, (and was initially believed to be their only show),<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.kerrang.com/blog/2012/04/exclusive_bring_me_the_horizon_2.html|title=Exclusive! Bring Me The Horizon for Warped Tour UK!|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=11 April 2012|access-date=5 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414103259/http://www.kerrang.com/blog/2012/04/exclusive_bring_me_the_horizon_2.html|archive-date=14 April 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> the [[BBC Radio 1]]'s ''Radio 1 Rocks'' show on 22 October, where they played a six-song set supporting [[Bullet for My Valentine]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/bullet-for-my-valentine-bring-me-the-horizon-while-she-sleeps-to-play-bbc-radio-1-rocks-event-this-month/|title=Bullet For My Valentine, Bring Me The Horizon, While She Sleeps To Play BBC Radio 1 Rocks Event This Month|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=10 October 2012|access-date=24 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025053236/http://www.metalhammer.co.uk/news/bullet-for-my-valentine-bring-me-the-horizon-while-she-sleeps-to-play-bbc-radio-1-rocks-event-this-month/|archive-date=25 On 4 January 2013, Bring Me the Horizon released the first single from ''Sempiternal'', "[[Shadow Moses (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Shadow Moses]]". It was first played by radio presenter [[Daniel P. Carter]] on BBC's Radio 1. Due to popular demand, [[Epitaph]] released the music video for the song a week earlier than planned.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=185202|title=Bring Me the Horizon: 'Shadow Moses' Video Released|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=22 January 2013|access-date=12 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130530115727/http://blabbermouth.net/news.aspx?mode=Article&newsitemID=185202|archive-date=30 May 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> In January, the band also saw a change in their line up. This began early in the month when [[Jordan Fish]], Worship [[keyboardist]] and session musician for the band during the writing of ''Sempiternal'', was announced as a full member. Then later in the month, Jona Weinhofen left the band for undisclosed reasons.<ref name="loudwire-jona left">{{cite web|first=Graham|last=Hartmann|url=http://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-confirm-departure-guitarist-jona-weinhofen/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Confirm Departure of Guitarist Jona Weinhofen|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=14 January 2013|access-date=12 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130219013744/http://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-confirm-departure-guitarist-jona-weinhofen/|archive-date=19 February 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> Despite the band denying speculation that Fish replaced Weinhofen,<ref name="loudwire-jona left" /> reviewers said that replacing a guitarist with a keyboardist better fit their style.<ref>{{cite podcast|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JazsH1u2QXU&list=PLt5p52djwaRzbfJ-Nyyuf_v2hgxhepYwa|title=Metal Hammer Podcast 230 Part 3: Bring Me The Horizon 'Sempiternal' Review|website=[[YouTube]] | publisher=[[Metal Hammer]] ([[Future plc]])|host=Merl, Hill and Amit|date=5 February 2013|time=5:20|access-date=12 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053825/http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JazsH1u2QXU&list=PLt5p52djwaRzbfJ-Nyyuf_v2hgxhepYwa|archive-date=21 September 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

===''That's the Spirit'' (2015–2017)===
{{Main|That's the Spirit}}
In late June, the band began to promote pictures of an umbrella symbol being used as a tattoo, and on stickers, and posters across England, the United States, Australia, and Europe; it was later used for a promotional cover for the band's first single.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Andy|last=Biddulph|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/what-are-bring-me-the-horizon-up-to|title=What Are Bring Me The Horizon Up To?|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|access-date=3 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052947/http://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/what-are-bring-me-the-horizon-up-to|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band released a short video in early July where the words "that's the spirit" could be heard in reverse.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=http://www.kerrang.com/33390/bring-horizon-release-teaser-video/|title=Bring Me The Horizon Unveil Teaser Video|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=6 July 2015|access-date=3 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322102039/http://www.kerrang.com/33390/bring-horizon-release-teaser-video/|archive-date=22 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 21 October 2014, released the single, "[[Drown (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Drown]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_release_drown_music_video/|title=Bring Me The Horizon release "Drown" music video|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=21 October 2014|access-date=6 June 2024}}</ref> On 13 July 2015, the second single "[[Happy Song (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Happy Song]]" was released,<ref>{{cite web|first=Anya|last=Zadrozny|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-happy-song-oli-sykes-gets-married/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Unleash 'Happy Song,' Frontman Oli Sykes Gets Married|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=13 July 2015|access-date=6 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240605095650/https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-happy-song-oli-sykes-gets-married/|archive-date=5 June 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> and on 21 July 2015, Sykes revealed the album's name was ''[[That's the Spirit]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gavin|last=Haynes|url=https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/bring-me-the-horizon-on-new-album-thats-the-spirit-and-riding-around-greek-islands-on-quad-bikes|title=Bring Me The Horizon On New March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The band released the single and music video for "[[Throne (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Throne]]" on 24 July 2015.<ref>{{cite web|first=David|last=Renshaw|url=https://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/87105|title=Bring Me The Horizon reveal new single 'Throne' – watch|work=[[NME]]|date=24 July 2015|access-date=6 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160522222558/https://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/87105|archive-date=22 May 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The next single, "True Friends", was released on 24 August 2015.<ref>{{cite web|first=Anya|last=Zadrozny|url=http://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-true-friends/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Unleash New Song 'True Friends'|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=24 August 2015|access-date=3 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304133744/http://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-true-friends/|archive-date=4 web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/video-premiere-bring-me-the-horizons-follow-you/|title=Video Premiere: Bring Me The Horizon's 'Follow You'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=16 March 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> The music video for the next single, "[[Avalanche (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Avalanche]]", was released on 23 June 2016.<ref>{{cite web|first=Stef|last=Lach|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-in-avalanche-video|title=Bring Me The Horizon in Avalanche video|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=24 June magazine|first=Chris|last=Payne|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/bring-me-the-horizon-oh-no-video-oli-sykes-thats-the-spirit-7565512/|title=Unravel the Mystery of a Trumpet-Playing Alien Baby The band embarked on a U.S. tour in October 2015 with support from [[Issues (band)|Issues]] and [[PVRIS]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=http://www.kerrang.com/34320/pvris-join-bring-me-the-horizon-issues-tour/|title=PVRIS Join Bring Me The Horizon/Issues US Tour|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|date=3 August 2015|access-date=3 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161109213129/http://www.kerrang.com/34320/pvris-join-bring-me-the-horizon-issues-tour/|archive-date=9 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The band also toured Europe in November 2015, and embarked on a second U.S. tour in April and May 2016. This was followed by  an Australian tour in September 2016, and a second European tour in November 2016.<ref>{{cite web|first=Graham|last=Hartmann|url=http://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-2016-u-s-tour-dates/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Announce Spring 2016 U.S. Tour Dates|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=22 February 2016|access-date=3 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160703025053/http://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-2016-u-s-tour-dates/|archive-date=3 July 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-horizon-announce-2016-australian-tour/|title=Bring Me The Horizon Announce 2016 Australian Tour|magazine=[[Music Feeds]]|date=17 February 2016|access-date=3 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160425134016/http://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-horizon-announce-2016-australian-tour/|archive-date=25 April 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 22 April 2016, the band performed a live concert with an orchestra conducted by [[Simon Dobson]] at the [[Royal Albert Hall]] in London. The concert marked the first time the band had performed with a live orchestra. It was recorded, and the live album, ''[[Live at the Royal Albert Hall (Bring Me the Horizon album)|Live at the Royal Albert Hall]]'', was released on 2 December 2016 through the crowdfunding platform [[PledgeMusic]] on CD, DVD, and vinyl, with all proceeds donated to [[Teenage Cancer Trust]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.teenagecancertrust.org/bring-me-horizon-announced-our-2016-royal-albert-hall-shows|title=Bring Me The Horizon announced for our 2016 Royal Albert Hall shows|work=Teenage Cancer 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Luke Morgan Britton|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-14-1190889|title=Bring Me The Horizon announce Teenage Cancer Trust show at London's Royal Albert Hall|work=[[NME]]|date=27 November 2015|access-date=6 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809111814/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-14-1190889|archive-date=9 August 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Stef|last=Lach|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-ponder-orchestra-tour|title=Bring Me The Horizon ponder orchestra tour|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=27 April ===''Amo'' (2018–2019)===
{{Main|Amo (Bring Me the Horizon album)|l1=Amo}}
In August 2018, cryptic posters appeared in major cities throughout the world with the message "do you wanna start a cult with me?".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/bring-me-the-horizons-cult-posters-have-turned-up-in-chicago/|title=Bring Me the Horizon's "Cult" Posters Have Turned Up in Chicago|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=18 August 2018|access-date=17 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817225434/https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/bring-me-the-horizons-cult-posters-have-turned-up-in-chicago/|archive-date=17 August 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> The posters were attributed by major media outlets to the band only by their use of the hexagram logo previously used by the band. During this time the band themselves have not acknowledged their involvement with the campaign publicly. Each poster provided a unique phone number and a website address.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://joinmantra.org/|title=An Invitation To Salvation|website=Join Mantra|access-date=17 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817193349/http://joinmantra.org/|archive-date=17 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The website provided a brief message titled "An Invitation To Salvation" and shows the date of 21 August 2018. The phone lines placed fans on hold with lengthy, varied audio messages that changed frequently.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Alex|last=Darus|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-mantra-cult-us/|title=Bring Me the Horizon's Cryptic Album Teasing Has Reached the US|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=13 August 2018|access-date=17 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107080616/https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-mantra-cult-us/|archive-date=7 November 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Some of these messages reportedly end with a distorted audio clip of what was assumed to be new music from the band.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Stephen|last=Ackroyd|url=https://www.upsetmagazine.com/news/it-looks-like-bring-me-the-horizon-are-teasing-something-new|title=It looks like Bring Me The Horizon are teasing something new|magazine=Upset Magazine|date=11 August 2018|access-date=1 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817193325/https://www.upsetmagazine.com/news/it-looks-like-bring-me-the-horizon-are-teasing-something-new|archive-date=17 August 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Bring me the Horizon - 2019159205442 2019-06-08 Rock am Ring - 2106 - AK8I0006.jpg|thumb|right|Bring Me the Horizon at Rock am Ring in 2019]]
On 21 August, the band released the lead single "[[Mantra (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Mantra]]".<ref name="rock sound mantra">{{cite magazine|first=Brii|last=Jamieson|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-amo-mantra-tour|title=Bring Me The Horizon Have Announced The Details Of Their New Album, Announced A Tour|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=22 August 2018|access-date=28 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829003300/https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-amo-mantra-tour|archive-date=29 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Blabbermouth mantra">{{cite web|url=https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-releases-music-video-for-mantra|title=Bring Me The Horizon Releases Music Video For 'Mantra'|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=24 August 2018|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602013209/https://blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-releases-music-video-for-mantra|archive-date=2 June 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The following day the band announced their album ''[[Amo (Bring Me the Horizon album)|Amo]]'', released on 11 January 2019, along with a set of tour dates called the First Love World Tour.<ref name="rock sound mantra"/><ref name="Blabbermouth mantra"/>

On 21 October, the band released their second single "[[Wonderful Life (Bring Me the Horizon song)|Wonderful Life]]" featuring [[Dani Filth]], along with the tracklist for ''Amo''.<ref name="alternative press wonderful life">{{cite magazine|first=Rachel|last=Campbell|url=https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-new-song-wonderful-life/|title=Bring Me The Horizon unleash "Wonderful Life", more album details|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=21 October 2018|access-date=22 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101042817/https://www.altpress.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-new-song-wonderful-life/|archive-date=1 November 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Morton|url=https://www.loudersound.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-release-new-song-wonderful-life-featuring-dani-filth|title=Bring Me The Horizon release new song Wonderful Life featuring Dani Filth|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=22 October 2018|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230602013207/https://www.loudersound.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon-release-new-song-wonderful-life-featuring-dani-filth|archive-date=2 June 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> That same day, the band announced that the album has been delayed and is now set for 25 January 2019.<ref name="alternative press wonderful life"/>

On 1 December, it was reported that during a show at London's Alexandra Palace a fan died in the [[mosh pit]] and was escorted by paramedics and security. A day later, it was confirmed by the band with a statement: "Words cannot express how horrified we are feeling this evening after hearing about the death of a young man at our show last night. Our hearts and deepest condolences go out to his family and loved ones at this terrible time. We will comment further in due course."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/report-fan-dies-in-the-pit-of-bring-me-the-horizon-show|title=Report fan dies in the pit of Bring Me The Horizon show|work=Metal Injection|date=1 December 2018|access-date=3 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181203095423/http://www.metalinjection.net/latest-news/report-fan-dies-in-the-pit-of-bring-me-the-horizon-show|archive-date=3 December 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-46441069|title=Bring Me The Horizon: Sister of fan who died at gig pays tribute|work=[[BBC]]|date=6 December 2018|access-date=10 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240214134739/https://www.bbc.com/news/newsbeat-46441069|archive-date=14 February 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

===''Post Human: Survival Horror'', ''Nex Gen'' and Fish's departure (2020–present)===
{{Main|Post Human: Survival Horror|Post Human: Nex Gen}}
During the [[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] lockdowns, the band shared that they were in a home studio, writing and recording material for their eighth record.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Skinner|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-to-live-stream-home-studio-footage-as-they-work-on-new-album-under-lockdown-2635030|title=Watch Bring Me The Horizon record their eighth album while under lockdown|work=[[NME]]|date=13 April 2020|access-date=21 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129035121/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-to-live-stream-home-studio-footage-as-they-work-on-new-album-under-lockdown-2635030|archive-date=29 January 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 June, the band released the single "[[Parasite Eve (song)|Parasite Eve]]" alongside an accompanying music video. On the same day, the band also announced a project that they have been working on titled ''Post Human'', which they said to be four EPs released throughout the next year which when combined would make an album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Trendell|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-post-human-new-album-oli-sykes-interview-2694847|title=Bring Me The Horizon tell us about their new 'survival horror song' 'Parasite Eve' and ambitious 'Post Human' project|work=[[NME]]|date=25 June 2020|access-date=25 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628070525/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-post-human-new-album-oli-sykes-interview-2694847|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Jackson|last=Langford|url=https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-me-the-horizon-are-planning-to-release-four-albums-over-the-next-year/|title=Bring Me The Horizon are planning to release four albums over the next year|work=[[Music Feeds]]|date=26 June 2020|access-date=26 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628103053/https://musicfeeds.com.au/news/bring-me-the-horizon-are-planning-to-release-four-albums-over-the-next-year/|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The song was produced by [[Doom Eternal]] composer, [[Mick Gordon (composer)|Mick Gordon]].<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Rachael|last=Dowd|url=https://www.altpress.com/bring-me-the-horizon-parasite-eve-video/|title=See Bring Me The Horizon enter a horrifying new world in "Parasite released with English singer [[Yungblud]] a collaborative single titled "[[Obey (Bring Me the Horizon and Yungblud song)|Obey]]" and its corresponding music video.<ref>{{cite web|first=Lauryn|last=Schaffner|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-yungblud-new-song-obey/|title=Bring Me the Horizon Drop New Song 'Obey' Featuring Yungblud|work=[[Loudwire]]|date=2 magazine|first=James|last=Wilson-Taylor|url=https://www.rocksound.tv/news/read/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-post-human-survival-horror|title=Bring Me The Horizon Just Announced A New Release – 'Post video.<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/the-news/bring-me-the-horizon-tease-new-song-tear-drops/|title=Bring Me The Horizon Tease New Song, Tear In December 2020, Fish said that the band had been writing "on and off" and would be focusing on their next release in early 2021. He also updated the group's release plan, saying that they "planned to do four EPs in a year, but [''Post Human: Survival Horror''] was almost an album, so I think the spacing will be a bit longer than intended, just because they're probably going to turn out bigger than intended."<ref>{{cite interview|first=Jordan|last=Fish|interviewer=Nick Ruskell|url=https://www.kerrang.com/features/bring-me-the-horizon-jordan-fish-my-year-2020/|title=Bring Me The Horizon's Jordan Fish: "My dream is to play live for three hours"|publisher=Wasted Talent|date=28 December 2020|magazine=[[Kerrang!]]|access-date=31 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230212600/https://www.kerrang.com/features/bring-me-the-horizon-jordan-fish-my-year-2020/|archive-date=30 December 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Upon being released on physical formats on 22 January 2021, ''Post Human: Survival Horror'' would chart again and reach a new peak to gift Bring Me the Horizon their second UK number one on the [[UK Albums Chart]]. Two years after ''Amo'' would be the first to reach this feat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://store.hmv.com/store/music/cd/post-human-survival-horror|title=Post Human: Survival Horror – Bring Me the Horizon|publisher=[[HMV]]|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210410145452/https://store.hmv.com/store/music/cd/post-human-survival-horror|archive-date=10 April 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Helen|last=Ainsley|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/bring-me-the-horizon-score-their-second-number-1-album-with-post-human-survival-horror-it-feels-like-a-really-exciting-time-for-us-__32332/|title=Bring Me The Horizon score their second Number 1 album with Post Human: Survival Horror: "It feels like a really exciting time for us"|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|date=29 January 2021|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205021559/https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/bring-me-the-horizon-score-their-second-number-1-album-with-post-human-survival-horror-it-feels-like-a-really-exciting-time-for-us-__32332/|archive-date=5 February 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> The band collaborated with singer [[Olivia O'Brien]] on a track titled "No More Friends". The song is from O'Brien's ''Episodes: Season 1' EP'' which was released on 11 June 2021.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Reilly|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizons-oli-sykes-teams-up-with-olivia-obrien-on-new-track-no-more-friends-2967212|title=Bring Me The Horizon's Oli Sykes teams up with Olivia O'Brien on new track 'No More Friends'|work=[[NME]]|date=11 June 2021|access-date=12 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210612190612/https://www.nme.com/news/music/bring-me-the-horizons-oli-sykes-teams-up-with-olivia-obrien-on-new-track-no-more-friends-2967212|archive-date=12 June 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Artistry==

===Style and influences===

Among Bring Me the Horizon's earliest influences were bands like [[At the Gates]], [[Carcass (band)|Carcass]], [[Pantera]], [[Metallica]], [[Zao (American band)|Zao]], [[Arch Enemy]], [[The Dillinger Escape Plan]], [[Every Time I Die]], [[Norma Jean (band)|Norma Jean]], [[Skycamefalling]], [[Slipknot (band)|Slipknot]] and [[Poison the Well (band)|Poison the Well]];{{sfn|Patterson|2011|p=45}}<ref name="rockfreaks 1"/><ref name="Rocksound-olis mind"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-replaces-bury-your-dead-on-killswitch-engage-s-european-tour/|title=Bring Me The Horizon Replaces Bury Your Dead On Killswitch Engage's European Tour|work=[[Blabbermouth.net]]|date=7 January 2007|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160508213812/http://www.blabbermouth.net/news/bring-me-the-horizon-replaces-bury-your-dead-on-killswitch-engage-s-european-tour/|archive-date=8 May 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=MusicRadar>{{cite web|url=http://www.musicradar.com/news/drums/matt-nicholls-bring-me-the-horizon-interview-580345|title=Matt Nicholls (Bring Me The Horizon) interview|work=[[MusicRadar]]|date=31 July 2013|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150910230523/http://www.musicradar.com/news/drums/matt-nicholls-bring-me-the-horizon-interview-580345|archive-date=10 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Kennelty|url=https://metalinjection.net/news/corey-taylor-recalls-discovering-bring-me-the-horizon-after-they-covered-eyeless|title=Corey Taylor Recalls Discovering Bring Me The Horizon After They Covered "Eyeless"|work=Metal Injection|date=30 October 2021|access-date=16 September 2025|quote=Obviously we all love Slipknot, we owe, like, you know, Bring Me the Horizon would not be here if Slipknot didn't exist, the first drum kit we ever got was the Corey Taylor kit|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240621201600/https://metalinjection.net/news/corey-taylor-recalls-discovering-bring-me-the-horizon-after-they-covered-eyeless|archive-date=21 June 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> and genres [[death metal]] like "[[Decapitated (band)|Decapitated]] or [[Suffocation (band)|Suffocation]]",<ref name="auto">{{cite web|first=Philip|last=Trapp|url=https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-oli-sykes-names-band-that-first-got-him-into-metal/|title=Oli Sykes Names the Album That First Got Him Into 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161055/https://loudwire.com/bring-me-the-horizon-oli-sykes-names-band-that-first-got-him-into-metal/|archive-date=1 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> [[grindcore]], and [[emo]] have been cited by [[AllMusic]] writer Steward Mason.<ref name="allmusic bio">{{cite web|first=Stewart|last=Mason|url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/bring-me-the-horizon-p831398/biography|title=Bring Me the Horizon Allmusic|work=[[AllMusic]]|access-date=26 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110519130740/http://allmusic.com/artist/bring-me-the-horizon-p831398/biography|archive-date=19 May 2011|url-status=live}}</ref> However, as their sound developed, the band started to take influences from [[progressive rock]], [[post-rock]], [[dubstep]] and [[electronica]].{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=52}}<ref name="Rocksound-olis mind">{{cite magazine|first=Ben|last=Patashnik|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/features/article/inside-the-mind-of-oliver-sykes|title=Inside The Mind Of Oliver Sykes|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=28 September 2010|access-date=30 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120918115238/http://www.rocksound.tv/features/article/inside-the-mind-of-oliver-sykes|archive-date=18 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> According to Eli Enis of ''[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]'', the band "made chameleonic genre-hopping their artistic mission statement."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Eli|last=Enis|url=https://www.revolvermag.com/music/15-great-bands-sound-totally-different-their-debut-albums/|title=15 Great Bands That Sound Totally Different From Their Debut Albums|magazine=[[Revolver (magazine)|Revolver]]|date=21 March 2022|access-date=22 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415230537/https://www.revolvermag.com/music/15-great-bands-sound-totally-different-their-debut-albums/|archive-date=15 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> 

In an interview with ''[[NME]]'', Sykes said that ''[[That's the Spirit]]'' is a loose [[concept album]] about life's darker moods, such as depression, and a way of making light of it. He cited the [[alternative rock]] bands [[Jane's Addiction]], [[Panic! at the Disco]], [[Interpol (band)|Interpol]] and [[Radiohead]] as influences for the new album.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gavin|last=Haynes|url=https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/bring-me-the-horizon-on-new-album-thats-the-spirit-and-riding-around-greek-islands-on-quad-bikes-16314|title=Bring Me The Horizon On New Album 'That's The Spirit' - And Riding Around Greek Islands On Quad Bikes|work=[[NME]]|date=21 July 2015|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240610030730/https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/bring-me-the-horizon-on-new-album-thats-the-spirit-and-riding-around-greek-islands-on-quad-bikes-16314|archive-date=10 June 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> They also cited [[Twenty One Pilots]] as an influence on the band's "next phase".<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Maggie|last=Dickman|url=https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_twenty_one_pilots_influence_new_music/|title=Bring Me The Horizon talk new music, cite Twenty One Pilots as influence|magazine=[[Alternative Press (magazine)|Alternative Press]]|date=8 March 2018|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161055/https://www.altpress.com/bring_me_the_horizon_twenty_one_pilots_influence_new_music/|archive-date=1 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref>

Oliver Sykes also said that his vocal style on Sempiternal was influenced by [[Chester Bennington]] and cited ''[[Hybrid Theory]]'' as one of his favorite albums.<ref>{{cite web|first=Merlin|last=Aldersladelast|url=https://www.loudersound.com/features/oli-sykes-the-10-albums-that-changed-my-life|title=Bring Me The Horizon's Oli Sykes: 10 albums that changed my life|work=[[Metal Hammer]]|date=30 January 2019|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401161055/https://www.loudersound.com/features/oli-sykes-the-10-albums-that-changed-my-life|archive-date=1 April 2024|url-status=live}}</ref> The album that got him to metal was [[Alive or Just Breathing]] by [[Killswitch Engage]].<ref name="auto"/> Jordan Fish said that the albums that influenced him most were [[Linkin Park]]'s ''Hybrid Theory'' and [[Deftones]]' ''[[White Pony]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first=Emily|last=Carter|url=https://www.kerrang.com/how-linkin-park-are-influencing-bring-me-the-horizons-new-music/|title=How Linkin Park Are Influencing Bring Me The Horizon's New Music|work=[[Kerrang!]]|date=13 October 2020|access-date=16 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720180950/https://www.kerrang.com/how-linkin-park-are-influencing-bring-me-the-horizons-new-music/|archive-date=20 July 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

The band's musical style has been described mainly as [[metalcore]] and – though they have since moved on from the genre – their early material was considered [[deathcore]].{{refn|group=note|Musical styles:{{columns-list|

Bring Me the Horizon have attempted to grow and change with each album, believing they should be different.<ref name="RS-classic BFMV">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/bring-me-the-head-of-british-metal-revisited?|title=Rock Sound Classic Interviews: Matt Tuck vs Oli Sykes|magazine=[[Rock Sound]]|date=21 March 2013|access-date=6 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812095853/http://www.rocksound.tv/features/read/bring-me-the-head-of-british-metal-revisited|archive-date=12 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Raziq Rauf, writing for ''[[Drowned in Sound]]'', described ''Count Your Blessings'' as possessing "Norma Jean-style thunderous riffs mixed with some dastardly [[Sludge metal|sludgy]] [[Doom metal|doom]] moments and more [[breakdowns (music)|breakdowns]] than your dad's old Nissan Sunny."<ref name="Dis-party music"/> ''[[Metal Hammer]]'' described ''Suicide Season'' as a "creative, critical and commercial success" for the band{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=52}} as they started to adopt a more eclectic style,<ref name="DIS-bio">{{cite web|url=http://drownedinsound.com/artists/Bring_Me_The_Horizon|title=Bring Me The Horizon // Drowned In Sound|work=[[Drowned In Sound]]|access-date=20 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919010404/http://drownedinsound.com/artists/Bring_Me_The_Horizon|archive-date=19 September 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> with its "crushingly heavy party deathcore".{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=50}} Leading up to its release, Oliver Sykes described it as "100% different to ''Count Your Blessings''" and noted the album sounds "more rock than metal".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.killyourstereo.com/news/1730/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-info/|title=Bring Me The Horizon new album info|work=Kill Your Stereo|date=27 August 2008|access-date=28 July 2012|quote="100% different" from "Count Your Blessings" [...] "More rock than metal. It's heavy though, and sounds a lot more fatter and beefier. We've also done some mellower tracks too."|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921053437/http://www.killyourstereo.com/news/1730/bring-me-the-horizon-new-album-info/|archive-date=21 September 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> As time went by, Bring Me the Horizon began rejecting their debut album ''Count Your Blessings'' and considered ''Suicide Season'' as their "Year Zero[...] ''[their]'' wipe-the-slate-clean time".{{sfn|Gill|2010|p=53}}

Bring Me the Horizon then moved even further away from deathcore with their third album ''[[There Is a Hell Believe Me I've Seen It. There Is a Heaven Let's Keep It a Secret.|There Is a Hell...]]'', which incorporated electronica, classical music and pop music into their metalcore style.<ref name="CANOE-horizons broadened">{{cite web|first=Darryl|last=Sterdan|url=http://jam.canoe.ca/Music/Artists/B/Bring_Me_The_Horizon/2010/11/18/16203866.html|title=Horizon broadens for young band|work=[[QMI Agency]]|publisher=[[Canoe Inc.]]|date=18 November 2010|access-date=20 March 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121209031552/http://jam.canoe.ca/Music/Artists/B/Bring_Me_The_Horizon/2010/11/18/16203866.html|archive-date=9 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> This required more ambitious production feats, such as using a full [[choir]], a synthesised [[orchestra]] and glitched out vocals and breakdowns that were also toned down, favouring quiet atmospheric passages in song breaks.<ref name="Allmusic-TIAH Review">{{cite web|first=Gregory|last=Heaney|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/there-is-a-hell-believe-me-ive-seen-it-there-is-a-heaven-lets-keep-it-a-secret-r1951223/review|title=There Is a Hell, Believe Me I've Seen It, There is a Heaven, Let's Keep It a Secret – Bring Me the Horizon|work=[[Allmusic]]|access-date=14 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101016090736/http://www.allmusic.com/album/there-is-a-hell-believe-me-ive-seen-it-there-is-a-heaven-lets-keep-it-a-secret-r1951223/review|archive-date=16 October 2010|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="UG-Lee Guitar interview">{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Matera|url=http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/interviews/interviews/bring_me_the_horizon_interview_with_the_guitarist_lee_malia.html|title=Bring Me The Horizon: Interview With The Guitarist Lee Malia|work=[[Ultimate Guitar]]|date=11 February 2011|access-date=11 May 2012|quote=Yet, the album still includes the trademark elements that have become staples of the group's sound since 2006 – precision guitar riffs, venomously dark lyrics, massive breakdowns and gang vocals destined to be chants at the band's incendiary live shows. [...] We always thought 'why should we stick to the two guitars, drums and bass format? Why can't we have some production stuff brought into it and look at each song as a bigger picture?|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309190818/http://www.ultimate-guitar.com/interviews/interviews/bring_me_the_horizon_interview_with_the_guitarist_lee_malia.html|archive-date=9 March 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> For the writing of ''[[Sempiternal (album)|Sempiternal]]'', the band pooled far broader influences such as post-rock acts like [[This Will Destroy You]] and [[Explosions in the Sky]]<ref name="NME 3">{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Goodwyn|url=https://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/61173|title=Bring Me the Horizon Planning 'Post-Rock' Influenced Fourth Album|work=[[NME]]|date=29 December 2011|access-date=3 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120103090538/http://www.nme.com/news/bring-me-the-horizon/61173|archive-date=3 January 2012|url-status=live}}</ref> and from pop music.<ref name="AD-Sempiternal/Movies">{{cite web|first=Rick|last=Florino|url=http://www.artistdirect.com/entertainment-news/article/oli-sykes-of-bring-me-the-horizon-talks-sempiternal-movies-and-more/10565341|title=Oli Sykes of Bring Me The Horizon Talks "Sempiternal", Movies, and More|work=[[Artistdirect]]|date=20 May 2013|access-date=21 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609072721/http://www.artistdirect.com/entertainment-news/article/oli-sykes-of-bring-me-the-horizon-talks-sempiternal-movies-and-more/10565341|archive-date=9 June 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>
