'''Lifehouse''' is an American [[rock music|rock]] band from [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] composed of [[Jason Wade]] (lead vocals, rhythm guitar, piano), [[Rick Woolstenhulme Jr.]] (drums, percussion), [[Bryce Soderberg]] (bass, vocals), and Steve Stout (lead guitar). The band came to mainstream prominence with their 2000 single "[[Hanging by a Moment]]," which led their debut studio album, ''[[No Name Face]]'' (2000).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://top40.about.com/od/l/p/Lifehouse.htm|title=Lifehouse|last=Wolfe|first=Daniel|publisher=The New York Times Company|access-date=August 5, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825201301/http://top40.about.com/od/l/p/Lifehouse.htm|archive-date=August 25, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="About.com Article">{{cite web|url=http://top40.about.com/od/top10lists/tp/top10summer2001.htm|title=Top 10 Pop Songs – Summer 2001|last=Lamb|first=Bill|publisher=[[The New York Times Company]]|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref> The song peaked at number two on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], won a ''Billboard'' Music Award for [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2001|Hot 100 Single of the Year]]—having spent 20 weeks within the top ten and over a cumulative year on the chart<ref>{{cite web|url=http://longboredsurfer.com/charts.php?year=2001 |title=Billboard Top 100 – 2001 |access-date=July 24, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304120640/http://longboredsurfer.com/charts.php?year=2001 |archive-date=March 4, 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://top40.about.com/od/top100lists/tp/Top-100-Pop-Songs-Of-2001.09.htm|title=Top 100 Best Pop Songs of 2001|last=Lamb|first=Bill|publisher=[[The New York Times Company]]|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref>—and was named the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 2001|best-performing single of 2001]] despite not reaching the top position, making it the fourth song in the chart's history to do so.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://longboredsurfer.com/charts/2001.php | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100726111319/http://longboredsurfer.com/charts/2001.php | archive-date=July 26, 2010 | title=Billboard Top 100 - 2001 - Longbored Surfer - Charts }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/hot-100-60th-anniversary|title=Billboard Hot 100 60th Anniversary Interactive Chart|magazine=Billboard|access-date=February 14, 2020}}</ref>

The band has released six subsequent albums — ''[[Stanley Climbfall]]'' (2002), their [[Lifehouse (album)|eponymous third album]] (2005), ''[[Who We Are (Lifehouse album)|Who We Are]]'' (2007), ''[[Smoke & Mirrors (Lifehouse album)|Smoke and Mirrors]]'' (2010), ''[[Almería (album)|Almería]]'' (2012), and ''[[Out of the Wasteland]]'' (2015). Each were met with similar albeit trailing commercial success, spawning the singles "[[You and Me (Lifehouse song)|You and Me]]," "[[First Time (Lifehouse song)|First Time]]," and "[[Whatever It Takes (Lifehouse song)|Whatever It Takes]]" — each became hits on the [[Pop Airplay|Mainstream Top 40]], [[Adult Top 40]], and [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] charts, as well as the ''Billboard'' Hot 100.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/artist/307174/lifehouse/chart|title=Lifehouse – Chart History|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref> Lifehouse is exemplary of the [[adult contemporary music|adult contemporary]] format, meaning the band's songs are often played at public, family-oriented [[retail]] venues including [[supermarkets]], [[convention center]]s, and [[shopping mall|malls]].<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/adult-contemporary-radio-hits-millennials-724945/ | title=Adult Radio Was Once the Butt of Jokes. Now It's the Hottest Radio Format | magazine=[[Rolling Stone]] | date=October 20, 2018 }}</ref>

==History==
===1996–1999: Blyss and formation===
[[Jason Wade]] had been writing songs as a coping mechanism since his parents' divorce. After moving to Los Angeles in 1995, he met bassist Sergio Andrade, his next-door neighbor.<ref name="Wolfe">{{cite web|url=http://top40.about.com/od/l/p/Lifehouse.htm|title=Lifehouse|last=Wolfe|first=Daniel|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=August 5, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825201301/http://top40.about.com/od/l/p/Lifehouse.htm|archive-date=August 25, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following year, Wade, Andrade, and Jon "Diff" Palmer formed Blyss, the forerunner of Lifehouse, and began to play live shows at high schools and colleges.<ref name="Wolfe"/><ref name="IMDB">{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1654377/bio|title=Jason Wade (II) – Biography|publisher=[[IMDb]]|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref><ref name="JesusFreakHideout">{{cite web|url=http://www.jesusfreakhideout.com/interviews/Lifehouse2006.asp|title=Lifehouse Interview 2006|website=Jesusfreakhideout.com|access-date=January 16, 2016}}</ref> Later, Collin Hayden and Aaron Lord were added to the band.<ref name="IdolMe">{{cite web|url=http://www.idolme.com/artist/lifehouse.html|title=Lifehouse Biography|publisher=IdolMe.com|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref>

Soon thereafter, word-of-mouth reached producer [[Ron Aniello]], who introduced Jason to [[Jude Cole]], who in turn introduced him to [[DreamWorks Records]] principal Michael Ostin.<ref name="IMDB"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nctimes.com/entertainment/music/article_4670fce4-d32a-5f12-9f7a-82ac75b12538.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130208133725/http://www.nctimes.com/entertainment/music/article_4670fce4-d32a-5f12-9f7a-82ac75b12538.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 8, 2013|title=Lifehouse responds to low point with vigor|last=Moeller|first=Sean|publisher=[[North County Times]]|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref> In 1998, Aniello produced Blyss's first demos, with the financial backing of DreamWorks Records. Some of these recordings would form the 1999 EP ''[[Diff's Lucky Day]]'', which would be sold at live concerts or distributed among friends and music industry contacts.<ref name="IdolMe"/>

===2000–2001: ''No Name Face''===
{{Main|No Name Face}}
In 2000, Blyss re-recorded, remixed, and released 12 of the 15 ''Diff's Lucky Day'' session demos as ''[[No Name Face]]'', their debut major label release under the name of Lifehouse.<ref name="JesusFreakHideout"/><ref name="IdolMe"/> On their choosing the band name, frontman Jason Wade said, "It's about what we do as a band and for me personally. Most of this record is about my life and about life's circumstances. Not only my life, but other people's lives. We thought Lifehouse was a good name for it."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.concertlivewire.com/interviews/lifehouse.htm|title=Lifehouse Sees the Summit: Livewire's Exclusive Interview with Jason Wade of Lifehouse|publisher=Concert Livewire|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref> 

''No Name Face'' met significant commercial success and established the band, and eventually would sell in excess of four million copies worldwide.<ref name="IMDB"/> This was in part due to the success of "[[Hanging by a Moment]]", Lifehouse's first commercial single. Due to the charisma and talent of frontman Wade, DreamWorks Records' focus was primarily on him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Lifehouse/e/B000AR7ZRO/ref=ac_dpt_sa_link|title=Amazon.com: Lifehouse: Bio|publisher=Amazon.com|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref> "Hanging by a Moment" was the third song in chart history to be named the "No. 1 Song of the Year" on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] despite not having reached No. 1 on any weekly ''Billboard'' Hot 100 survey (after [[Sam the Sham|Sam the Sham & The Pharaohs]]' "[[Wooly Bully]]" in 1965 and [[Faith Hill]]'s "[[Breathe (Faith Hill song)|Breathe]]" in 2000).{{citation needed|date=May 2019}} The second single from the album, "[[Sick Cycle Carousel]]", was not as commercially successful as "Hanging by a Moment", peaking at No. 21 on the ''Billboard'' Modern Rock chart; the third and final single was "[[Breathing (Lifehouse song)|Breathing]]", a reworking of a song featured on ''Diff's Lucky Day''.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

The song "Everything" was the first of many Lifehouse songs to be featured in [[The WB]]'s future hit series ''[[Smallville (TV series)|Smallville]]''.<ref name="IdolMe"/> It was used in the [[Pilot (Smallville)|series pilot]] and [[Tempest (Smallville)|season 1 finale]], and again in the series' 200th episode "Homecoming" in the show's [[Smallville (season 10)|10th and final season]], as an homage to its [[Smallville (season 1)|season 1]] episodes nine years prior.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kryptonsite.com/smallvillemusicseason1.htm|title=KryptonSite's Smallville Music Guide: Season 1|publisher=KryptonSite.com|access-date=August 5, 2012}}</ref> The song "[[You and Me (Lifehouse song)|You and Me]]" from the band's [[Lifehouse (album)|eponymous third album]] would be released on Smallville's second [[soundtrack]], ''[[Smallville: The Metropolis Mix]]'', in an extended form subtitled "You and Me (Wedding Version)", and the band itself would perform the song live as a [[guest appearance|special guest appearance]] in the [[school prom]] scene at the end of the [[Smallville (season 4)|season 4]] episode "Spirit". Seven of the band's songs would be featured in episodes of the series' first four seasons.

The song "Somewhere in Between", also from ''No Name Face,'' was featured in the first-season episode of ''[[Falcon Beach]]'', "The Blame Game".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.falconbeach.ca/index.aspx?go=/episode_108.aspx |title=The official Falcon Beach website |publisher=Falconbeach.ca |date=December 4, 1999 |access-date=August 17, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728004537/http://www.falconbeach.ca/index.aspx?go=%2Fepisode_108.aspx |archive-date=July 28, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

By the time Lifehouse's first album was released, Palmer had left the band, and Wade and Andrade were the only remaining founding members.<ref name="IMDB"/> Soon after recording ''No Name Face'', Wade and Andrade met [[Rick Woolstenhulme]], who auditioned for the needed drummer part and joined the band as full-time drummer.<ref name="IMDB"/> Before the audition, Woolstenhulme had been rehearsing in an adjacent room to Lifehouse and frequently he and Wade would pass each other without meeting the other.<ref name="JesusFreakHideout"/>

=== 2002–2004: ''Stanley Climbfall'' ===
{{Main|Stanley Climbfall}}
Shortly after a long tour for ''No Name Face'', Lifehouse reentered the studio to cut their second album, ''Stanley Climbfall''. The album's initial success was short-lived and its singles, 2002's "[[Spin (song)|Spin]]" and 2003's "[[Take Me Away (Lifehouse song)|Take Me Away]]", were vastly overshadowed by the success of the first album.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://top40.about.com/od/l/p/Lifehouse.htm|title=Top 40 About: Lifehouse|access-date=January 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825201301/http://top40.about.com/od/l/p/Lifehouse.htm|archive-date=August 25, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Shortly after the album debuted, Rick's brother Sean Woolstenhulme (of [[The Calling (band)|The Calling]]) officially became the fourth member of the band in June 2002. He had previously toured with Lifehouse.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

In April 2004, Sergio Andrade confirmed that he had decided to leave the band to pursue individual projects. Shortly after his departure, Sean also left the band to pursue other musical projects such as [[Abandoned Pools]] and [[The Jimmy Chamberlin Complex]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcall.com/2005/05/27/new-moments-on-the-way-for-retooled-lifehouse/|title=New Moments on the Way for Retooled Lifehouse|website=Articles.mcall.com|date=May 27, 2005 |access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref>

===2004–2005: ''Lifehouse''===
{{Main|Lifehouse (album)}}
Jason Wade and Rick Woolstenhulme remained the active members of Lifehouse. In September 2004, [[Bryce Soderberg]] (previously of AM Radio) signed on as Lifehouse's new bassist. On July 6, 2004, they went to [[Maryland]] to begin work on their eponymous third album, spending less than two months in the studio to record thirteen songs produced by [[John Alagia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.popentertainment.com/lifehouse.htm|title=Lifehouse hanging on the charts|website=Popentertainment.com |date=May 28, 2005 |access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref> ''[[Lifehouse (album)|Lifehouse]]'' was released on March 22, 2005.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

The album's first single, "[[You and Me (Lifehouse song)|You and Me]]", was released for airplay on January 18, 2005. It was written several years prior and was originally performed by Jason Wade for the 2000 independent film ''All Over Again''. The song was a success and stayed on the U.S. ''Billboard'' Hot 100 for 62 weeks (the fifth longest-charted in history), peaking at No. 5.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}} The song also appears on the soundtrack to ''[[Smallville (TV series)|Smallville]]''. One episode, "Spirit", featured the band actually performing it and three other songs from the album ("Come Back Down", "Blind", and "Undone") on the show.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}} The song has also appeared on ''[[Cold Case (TV series)|Cold Case]]'', ''[[Boston Legal]]'', ''[[Gavin & Stacey]]'', ''[[Everwood]]'', ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'', ''[[The 4400]]'' and ''[[Medium (TV series)|Medium]]'' as well as the commercial for the final episode of ''[[Zoey 101]]''.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}} The song "All In All" was featured in ''[[Scrubs (TV series)|Scrubs]]''. The music video for the album's second single, "[[Blind (Lifehouse song)|Blind]]", was released October 19, 2005. It starred [[Tina Majorino]] and featured several other up-and-coming young actors such as Sarch McClain, Stephen Cheung, Christopher Thien Duc Van and Andy Walters.<ref name="JesusFreakHideout"/>

In 2006, the newly-written song "Good Enough" was featured in the [[Disney]] film ''[[The Wild]]'' and was repeated over the end credits.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405469/soundtrack|title=The Wild (2006) – Soundtracks|publisher=IMDb}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=May 2019}}

=== 2006–2008: ''Who We Are''===
[[File:LifehouseManila2.jpg|thumb|Lifehouse in 2008]]
{{Main|Who We Are (Lifehouse album)}}
Lifehouse began recording their fourth album in mid-2006 at [[Kiefer Sutherland]] and [[Jude Cole]]'s recording studio, Ironworks Studios in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1052523/lifehouse-returns-to-rock-on-who-we-are|title=Lifehouse Returns to Rock on 'Who We Are'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=April 27, 2007|access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref> Their fourth album, entitled ''Who We Are'', was released on June 19, 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lifehousemusic.com/discography/ |title=Lifehouse official discography |publisher=Lifehousemusic.com |access-date=August 17, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807135338/http://www.lifehousemusic.com/discography/ |archive-date=August 7, 2011  }}</ref> The album features Wade, Woolstenhulme and Soderberg as its lineup, and "rocks a little harder" than their previous album, according to the band.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx/nid/9368|title=It rocks a little harder – Lifehouse on ''Who We Are''|access-date=June 20, 2007|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070620213514/http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx/nid/9368|archive-date=June 20, 2007}}</ref> The album's release was followed by a tour with [[The Goo Goo Dolls]] and [[Colbie Caillat]], which began June 15 at the Dodge Theatre in [[Phoenix, AZ]].<ref name=whoweare>[http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx/nid/11170 The Moment we've all been waiting for] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070410024258/http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx/nid/11170 |date=April 10, 2007 }}: Lifehouse announces the title of their fourth album as ''Who We Are''.</ref>

The album's first single was a bright, pop rock love song "[[First Time (Lifehouse song)|First Time]]", released on April 24, 2007. The song debuted on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number 48 in May,<ref>Jonathan Cohen, [http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1052081/t-pain-tastes-hot-100-glory-with-drank "T. Pain Tastes Hot 100 Glory With 'Drank'"], Billboard.com, May 17, 2007.</ref> and peaked at number three on the Hot Adult Top 40 Charts. The album's second single, "[[Whatever It Takes (Lifehouse song)|Whatever It Takes]]" was released to radio stations on October 29, 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1047629/lifehouse-gets-serious-for-allstate-commercial |title=Lifehouse Gets Serious For Allstate Commercial |date=October 26, 2007 |publisher=Billboard.com |access-date=August 17, 2011}}</ref> "[[Broken (Lifehouse song)|Broken]]", the album's third single,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx/nid/15400 |title=Lifehouse Announces A Third Single |publisher=Lifehousemusic.com |date=April 15, 2011 |access-date=August 17, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716080702/http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx/nid/15400 |archive-date=July 16, 2011  }}</ref> peaked at number 83 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100. "Broken" has appeared on several television series, including ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'' ("Lay Your Hands On Me"), ''[[Criminal Minds]]'' ("In Birth and Death", season 3, episode 2), ''[[One Tree Hill (TV series)|One Tree Hill]]'', ''[[One Life to Live]]'' and ''[[The Hills (TV series)|The Hills]]''. Most recently, it was featured in the film soundtrack ''[[The Time Traveler's Wife (film)#Music|The Time Traveler's Wife]]''. 

Lifehouse held a contest to make a video for the song "Make Me Over".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.etonline.com/news/2008/04/61091/index.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080628143021/http://www.etonline.com/news/2008/04/61091/index.html|url-status=dead|title=Lifehouse Going Art House|archive-date=June 28, 2008|access-date=May 24, 2023}}</ref> The band gave 60 USC School of Cinematic Arts graduate students a chance to shoot the video for their new single. The winning video premiered at a gala event on December 5, 2008, at the Paley Center for Media in Beverly Hills, CA.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx?nid=17958 |title=Rock and Roll 'Em: Heineken Funds SCA Music Videos |publisher=Lifehousemusic.com |date=November 20, 2008 |access-date=August 17, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716080728/http://www.lifehousemusic.com/news/default.aspx?nid=17958 |archive-date=July 16, 2011  }}</ref>

The album was certified [[RIAA certification|Gold]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) in October 2008.<ref name=RIAA>{{cite web|url=https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&se=Lifehouse|title=Gold & Platinum – Lifehouse|publisher=[[Recording Industry Association of America]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304082435/https://www.riaa.com/gold-platinum/?tab_active=default-award&se=Lifehouse|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=live|access-date=April 28, 2022}}</ref>

=== 2008–2011: ''Smoke and Mirrors'' ===
{{Main|Smoke & Mirrors (Lifehouse album)}}
On April 11, 2009, the band announced that Ben Carey was an official member of the band. They said that they had been "a four-piece for some time" and that Ben is "family to us". Carey had been touring with the band since 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lifehousemusic.com/blog/default.aspx?nid=21119 |title=Lifehouse : Blog : Horseback riding |publisher=Lifehousemusic.com |date=July 28, 2007 |access-date=August 17, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110807140245/http://www.lifehousemusic.com/blog/default.aspx?nid=21119 |archive-date=August 7, 2011 }}</ref>

The single "[[Halfway Gone]]" was released on October 27, 2009. The music video premiered on the [[VH1]] Top 20 on VH1.com at the end of November.<ref>{{cite web|date=2009-11-23 |url=http://www.vh1.com/video/play.jhtml?id=1589364&vid=458409 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091204010807/http://www.vh1.com/video/play.jhtml?id%3D1589364%26vid%3D458409 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 4, 2009 |title="Halfway Gone" by Lifehouse &#124; Music Video |publisher=VH1.com |access-date=August 17, 2011}}</ref> ''[[Smoke & Mirrors (Lifehouse album)|Smoke & Mirrors]]'' was released on March 2, 2010.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=W.|first=M.|date=February 27, 2010|title=Reviews – Albums|magazine=Billboard|location=United States|publisher=Nielsen Business Media, Inc.|volume=122|issue=8|page=36|issn=0006-2510}}</ref> The album debuted at No. 6 on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] with 54,000 copies sold.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/959073/lady-antebellum-returns-to-no-1-on-billboard-200|title=Lady Antebellum Returns to No. 1 On Billboard 200|last=Caufield|first=Keith|date=March 10, 2010|magazine=Billboard|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141106140830/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/959073/lady-antebellum-returns-to-no-1-on-billboard-200|archive-date=November 6, 2014|url-status=live|access-date=Apr 28, 2022}}</ref> This marked the band's highest chart debut to date, surpassing their previous peak at No. 7 with ''[[Stanley Climbfall]]'' in 2002.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/lifehouse/chart-history/|title=Chart History – Lifehouse|magazine=Billboard|access-date=Apr 28, 2022}} (Note: Tap/click on down arrow and select "Billboard 200" from the drop-down menu to view chart history.)</ref>{{cbignore}}

===2011–2012: ''Almería''===
{{Main|Almería (album)}}
On September 11, 2012, Lifehouse released a new single featuring [[Natasha Bedingfield]] entitled "[[Between the Raindrops]]". A month later, on October 18, the band announced that the title of their sixth studio album would be ''Almería'', named after a city in Spain famous as the locale of many classic [[Spaghetti Western]] films.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ralphieaversa.com/2012/12/interview-lifehouse-gains-fans-and-haters-on-almeria/#.VGuSgIulmfc|title=INTERVIEW: Lifehouse Gains Fans and 'Haters' on 'Almeria'|work=ralphieaversa.com|access-date=January 15, 2015}}</ref> ''Almería'' was released on December 11 in the US and December 12 worldwide. The album was met with mixed reviews, and failed to spawn a second single.{{citation needed|date=May 2019}}

===2013–2018: ''Out of the Wasteland'' and ''Greatest Hits''===
{{Main|Out of the Wasteland}}
On July 24, 2013, Wade posted a letter to the band's [[Facebook]] page saying that Lifehouse had parted with Geffen and was on a temporary hiatus as each band member turned attention to other projects (with the assurance that the band would continue to make records in the future).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/lifehouse/posts/10151742035249025 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/facebook/18222514024/10151742035249025 |archive-date=2022-02-26 |url-access=limited|title=Lifehouse – A letter from Jason: To my friends and fans,... – Facebook|publisher=Facebook.com|access-date=January 15, 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Drummer [[Rick Woolstenhulme Jr.]] began touring with the [[Goo Goo Dolls]]; bassist [[Bryce Soderberg]] initiated a new band titled KOMOX; lead guitarist Ben Carey continued work in country rock band Elvis Monroe; and singer and songwriter [[Jason Wade]] worked on his as-yet-unreleased singer-songwriter solo record.<ref name="About Lifehouse">{{cite web|url=http://lifehousemusic.com/about/|title=About Lifehouse|publisher=Lifehouse Music|access-date=February 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206031908/http://lifehousemusic.com/about/|archive-date=February 6, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://themusicuniverse.com/goo-goo-dolls-part-ways-with-drummer-after-19-years|title=Goo Goo Dolls part ways with drummer after 19 years|website=Themusicuniverse.com|access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elvismonroe.com/#!who-we-are/c1gx2|title=Elvis Monroe|website=Elvismonroe.com|access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pledgemusic.com/artists/komox|title=Komox: Pledge Music|website=Pledgemusic.com|access-date=January 16, 2015}}</ref> The band's final show before their break was on September 25, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/lifehouse/photos/a.187202414024.122062.18222514024/10151877634254025/?type=1 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/facebook/18222514024/10151877634254025 |archive-date=2022-02-26 |url-access=limited|title=Lifehouse – Timeline Photos – Facebook|publisher=Facebook.com|access-date=January 15, 2015}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Lifehouse reentered the studio in May 2014. "[[Flight (Lifehouse song)|Flight]]" was released independently on November 18, along with an announcement that the band's hiatus was officially over and a new album entitled ''Seven'' would be released in April 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lifehousemusic.com/news/lifehouse-is-back-with-their-7th-studio-album/|title=Lifehouse is back with their 7th studio album|publisher=Lifehousemusic.com|access-date=January 19, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/lifehouse/status/550087749911728128|title=Lifehouse on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=January 15, 2015}}</ref> On December 8, 2014, Lifehouse stated on their official website that Ben Carey would no longer be a part of Lifehouse and instead would be focusing on his own projects; for live shows, the band later revealed that Steve Stout would fill in on lead guitar.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lifehousemusic.com/news/a-note-from-the-band/|title=Lifehouse A Note from the Band|author=The Uprising Creative|work=Lifehouse|access-date=January 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150116075824/http://lifehousemusic.com/news/a-note-from-the-band/|archive-date=January 16, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=May 2019}}

The album's first official single, "[[Hurricane (Lifehouse song)|Hurricane]]", was released on January 27, 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://creativeallies.com/contests/1002-design-an-album-cover-for-lifehouse-seven/more_info|title=Design An Album Cover for Lifehouse Seven|work=[[Creative Allies]]|access-date=January 15, 2015}}</ref> On January 27, ''Billboard''.com revealed a new album title ''Out of the Wasteland'' and published the official standard-edition track list of the album, giving an official release date of May 19, 2015.<ref name="About Lifehouse"/><ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/6451060/lifehouse-hurricane-video-exclusive-new-album|title=Exclusive: Lifehouse Premieres 'Hurricane' Video From 'Out of the Wasteland'|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=January 27, 2015|access-date=January 27, 2015}}</ref> The album was released online and in stores on May 26, 2015 and debuted at number one on the Independent Albums chart.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lifehousemusic.com/news/new-album-out-of-the-wasteland-debuts-at-1-on-independent-albums-chart|title=New Album Out of the Wasteland debuts at 1 on Independent Albums Chart|website=Lifehousemusic.com|date=June 10, 2015|access-date=June 23, 2015}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=May 2019}} A special [[Target Corporation|Target]] edition was made available with four bonus tracks.

The band was to begin touring in support of the album on June 19, as an opening act on the second North American leg of [[Nickelback]]'s [[No Fixed Address Tour]], before the tour was cancelled due to the health of Nickelback's lead singer, [[Chad Kroeger]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nickelback.com/news/title/medical-emergency-forces-cancellation-of-the-no-fixed-address-tour|title=Medical Emergency Forces Cancellation of the No Fixed Address Tour|website=Nickelback.com|date=June 23, 2015}}</ref> A European headlining tour commenced on September 15, 2015 in [[Amsterdam]], with extra dates added due to high demand.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lifehousemusic.com/tour|title=Lifehouse Tour Dates|website=Lifehousemusic.com|access-date=June 23, 2015}}</ref>

In June 2017, the band released their first Greatest Hits compilation, featuring all 17 of their radio singles to date in chronological order, plus one non-single that still charted on radio.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wnypapers.com/news/article/current/2017/06/08/128796/lifehouse-greatest-hits-multiplatinum-rock-bands-first-ever-compilation-set-for-release-july-14|title = 'Lifehouse: Greatest Hits,' multiplatinum rock band's first-ever compilation, set for release July 14|website=Wnypapers.com}}</ref> Lifehouse spent the summer of 2017 touring throughout the United States and Canada with [[Switchfoot]] in support of the album.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.livenation.com/artists/168801/lifehouse-switchfoot-looking-for-summer-tour|title=Lifehouse & Switchfoot Looking for Summer tour|website=Livenation.com|access-date=May 24, 2023}}</ref> It marked the first North American tour by the band since 2011. During the tour, Wade teamed up with [[Switchfoot]]'s [[Jon Foreman]], to help raise funds for Houston's [[Hurricane Harvey]] victims through the track called "Shine Like Gold".<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://people.com/music/lifehouse-switchfoot-single-shine-like-gold-raises-funds-hurricane-harvey-relief/|title=Lifehouse and Switchfoot Dropping New Single to Raise Funds for Hurricane Harvey Relief: 'We Love Houston'|website=People.com|access-date=April 2, 2018|language=en}}</ref>

In early 2018, Lifehouse toured with [[Collective Soul]] across South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigconcerts.co.za/events/detail/collective-soul-with-special-guest-lifehouse|title=Lifehouse & Collective Soul South African tour|website=Bigconcerts.co.za|access-date=May 24, 2023}}</ref>

[[File:Lifehouse at the 2019 Alameda County Fair (Quintin Soloviev).png|thumb|Lifehouse at the 2019 Alameda County Fair]]

=== 2019–present: Hiatus and ''Goodbye Kanan'' ===
Lifehouse released their first single in six years, "Cut & Run" in April 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|via=[[YouTube]]|title=Lifehouse - Cut & Run (Official Lyric Video)|date=April 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qniqsJsFkJs|language=en|access-date=2021-04-04}}</ref> The first single recorded with member Steve Stout, who had collaborated with Jason Wade on the side project ØZWALD and officially became the band's lead guitarist in 2017, the song was succeeded by four more singles over the course of 2021.<ref name="McGoldrick">{{cite web |last1=McGoldrick |first1=Meaghan |title=Concert Preview: Chart-topping rock band Lifehouse to "Search for Summer" at Ford Amphitheater in August |url=https://brooklynreporter.com/2017/07/chart-topping-rock-band-lifehouse-to-search-for-summer-at-coney-amphitheater-in-august/ |website=Brooklyn Reporter |access-date=April 15, 2021 |date=July 26, 2017}}</ref> The band compiled these five singles and one new track into their first EP, ''Goodbye Kanan'', released on November 26, 2021 under their own label Allswell Records.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.submithub.com/artist/lifehouse-1 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703121228/https://www.submithub.com/artist/lifehouse-1 | archive-date=July 3, 2022 | title=SubmitHub }}</ref>

==Other information==
Wade wrote the song "[[From Where You Are (Lifehouse song)|From Where You Are]]" for [[Allstate]]'s Teen Driving Program. The song was featured on the "Tall Lights" commercial and aired on NBC.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.idiomag.com/artist/lifehouse |title=Lifehouse Magazine – News, Reviews, Albums and Videos |website=Idiomag.com |access-date=August 17, 2011}}</ref>

==Band members==
=== Current members ===
*[[Jason Wade]] – lead vocals, rhythm guitar <small>(1995–present)</small>
*[[Rick Woolstenhulme Jr.]] – drums, percussion, occasional backing vocals <small>(2000–present)</small>
*[[Bryce Soderberg]] – bass guitar, backing and lead vocals <small>(2004–present)</small>
*Steve Stout – lead guitar, backing vocals <small>(2017–present; touring musician 2015–2017)</small>

=== Former members ===
*Aaron Lord – keyboards, violin, viola, mandolin, acoustic guitar <small>(1995–2000)</small>
*Jon "Diff" Palmer – drums, percussion <small>(1995–2000)</small>
*Collin Hayden – lead guitar <small>(1995–1999)</small>
*Tim Rhodes - lead guitar <small>(1999-2000)</small>
*Sergio Andrade – bass guitar <small>(1995–2004)</small>
*Sean Woolstenhulme – lead guitar, backing vocals <small>(2002–2004)</small>
*[[Ben Carey]] – lead guitar, backing vocals <small>(2009–2014; touring musician 2004–2009)</small>

==== Former touring musicians ====
*Stuart Mathis – lead guitar, backing vocals <small>(2000–2001)</small>
*Joerg Koehrig – lead guitar, backing vocals <small>(2001–2002)</small>

'''Sir Elton Hercules John''' (born '''Reginald Kenneth Dwight'''; 25 March 1947)<ref name="AllmusicBio">{{cite web |last=Erlewine |first=Stephen Thomas |title=Artist Biography [Elton John] |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/elton-john-mn0000796734/biography |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128200032/https://www.allmusic.com/artist/elton-john-mn0000796734/biography |archive-date=28 November 2020 |access-date=31 March 2014 |work=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref> is a British singer, songwriter and pianist. His music and showmanship have had a significant, lasting effect on the [[music industry]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/music/article/elton-johns-best-25-songs-ranked-from-daniel-to-your-song-kl27tg7vt |title=Elton John's best 25 songs ranked — from Daniel to Your Song |work=[[The Times]] |first=Jonathan |last=Dean |date=26 June 2023 | access-date=18 July 2023 | archive-date=18 July 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718224456/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/elton-johns-best-25-songs-ranked-from-daniel-to-your-song-kl27tg7vt | url-status=live}}</ref> and his songwriting partnership with lyricist [[Bernie Taupin]] is one of the most successful in history.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Elton John and Bernie Taupin {{!}} Songwriters Hall of Fame |url=https://www.songhall.org/awards/winner/elton_john_and_bernie_taupin |access-date=22 March 2022 |website=www.songhall.org |archive-date=24 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211024184254/https://www.songhall.org/awards/winner/elton_john_and_bernie_taupin |url-status=live }}</ref> John was the 19th [[EGOT]] winner in history. He has sold over 300 million records worldwide, making him one of the [[List of best-selling music artists|best-selling music artists of all time]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Savage |first1=Mark |date=24 January 2018 |title=BBC: Elton John to make statement on future |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-42804061 |url-status=live |access-date=15 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811070900/https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-42804061 |archive-date=11 August 2019}}</ref>

John learned to play piano at an early age, winning a scholarship to the [[Royal Academy of Music]]. In the 1960s, he formed the blues band [[Bluesology]], wrote songs for other artists alongside Taupin, and worked as a session musician, before releasing his debut album, ''[[Empty Sky]]'' (1969). Throughout the next six decades, John cemented his status as a [[cultural icon]] with [[Elton John albums discography|32 studio albums]], including ''[[Honky Château]]'' (1972), ''[[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road]]'' (1973), ''[[Rock of the Westies]]'' (1975), ''[[Sleeping with the Past]]'' (1989), ''[[The One (Elton John album)|The One]]'' (1992), ''[[Songs from the West Coast]]'' (2001), ''[[The Diving Board]]'' (2013) and ''[[The Lockdown Sessions (Elton John album)|The Lockdown Sessions]]'' (2021). His [[Elton John singles discography|catalog of hit singles]] includes "[[Your Song]]", "[[Tiny Dancer]]", "[[Rocket Man (song)|Rocket Man]]", "[[Crocodile Rock]]", "[[Bennie and the Jets]]", "[[Don't Go Breaking My Heart]]", "[[I'm Still Standing]]", "[[Sacrifice (Elton John song)|Sacrifice]]", "[[Can You Feel the Love Tonight]]" and "[[Cold Heart (Pnau remix)|Cold Heart]]". He has also had success in musical films and theatre, composing music for ''[[The Lion King]]'' (1994), ''[[Aida (musical)|Aida]]'' (2000), and ''[[Billy Elliot the Musical]]'' (2005). John's final tour, [[Farewell Yellow Brick Road]] (2018–2023), became the [[List of highest-grossing concert tours|highest-grossing tour ever]] at the time. His life and career were dramatised in the 2019 biopic ''[[Rocketman (film)|Rocketman]]''.

John is an [[HIV/AIDS]] charity fundraiser and has been involved in the fight against AIDS since the late 1980s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Elton John AIDS Foundation |url=http://www.ejaf.org/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208120655/http://ejaf.org/|archive-date=8 December 2019|access-date=6 August 2010 |publisher=Ejaf.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 July 2010 |title=Elton John: About: All About Elton: Charities |url=http://www.eltonjohn.com/about/charities.jsp |access-date=26 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100725061300/http://www.eltonjohn.com/about/charities.jsp |archive-date=25 July 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Our mission |url=https://www.eltonjohnaidsfoundation.org/about-us/our-mission/|access-date=26 January 2022 |website=Elton John AIDS Foundation |language=en-GB|archive-date=13 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213204329/https://www.eltonjohnaidsfoundation.org/about-us/our-mission/|url-status=live}}</ref> He established the [[Elton John AIDS Foundation]] in 1992, which has raised over £300&nbsp;million since its inception, and a year later he began hosting [[Elton John AIDS Foundation Academy Award Party|his annual AIDS Foundation Academy Awards Party]], which has since become one of the biggest high-profile Oscar parties in the [[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]] film industry.<ref name="Foundation">{{cite news |last=Butterworth |first=Benjamin |date=22 June 2019 |title=Sir Elton John emotional as he is awarded France's Legion d'Honneur for HIV Aids work |work=[[i (British newspaper)|i News]] |url=https://inews.co.uk/news/world/elton-john-aids-foundation-france-emmanuel-macron-award/ |url-status=live |access-date=8 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708205216/https://inews.co.uk/news/world/elton-john-aids-foundation-france-emmanuel-macron-award/ |archive-date=8 July 2019}}</ref> John was the chairman and director of [[Watford Football Club]] from 1976 to 1987, and again from 1997 to 2002, and is an honorary life president of the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ownership |url=https://www.watfordfc.com/club/ownership |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509041352/https://www.watfordfc.com/club/ownership |archive-date=9 May 2021 |access-date=6 May 2021 |publisher=Watford F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Yellow Brick Road: The Story Of Elton John & Watford FC |url=https://www.watfordfc.com/news/yellow-brick-road-the-story-of-elton-john-watford-fc |access-date=26 January 2022 |publisher=Watford F.C. |language=en |archive-date=26 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126002318/https://www.watfordfc.com/news/yellow-brick-road-the-story-of-elton-john-watford-fc |url-status=live}}</ref> From the late 1970s to the late 1980s, John developed a severe addiction to drugs and alcohol, but has been clean and sober since 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 June 2020 |title=Elton John Celebrates 30 Years of Sobriety |url=https://venturarecoverycenter.com/elton-john-sobriety/ |access-date=20 November 2022 |website=Ventura Recovery Center |language=en-US |archive-date=20 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221120163851/https://venturarecoverycenter.com/elton-john-sobriety/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2005, he entered a [[Civil partnership in the United Kingdom|civil partnership]] with his long-term partner, the Canadian filmmaker [[David Furnish]]. They married in 2014, when [[Same-sex marriage in the United Kingdom|same-sex marriage was legalised]] in England and Wales.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Corey |first=Irwin |title=The Day Elton John Married David Furnish |url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/elton-john-david-furnish/ |access-date=26 January 2022 |website=Ultimate Classic Rock |date=21 December 2020 |language=en |archive-date=15 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231215115642/https://ultimateclassicrock.com/elton-john-david-furnish/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

John has had more than fifty top-40 hits on the [[UK singles chart]] and US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], including nine number ones in both countries, as well as seven consecutive number-one albums in the US.<ref>{{cite news |title=Elton John |publisher=Official Charts Company |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/artist/21478/elton-john/ |url-status=live |access-date=5 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150309012348/http://www.officialcharts.com/artist/21478/ELTON-JOHN |archive-date=9 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Elton John on Being the Top Male Solo Artist of All Time |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/elton-john-top-male-solo-artist-interview/ |url-status=live |magazine=Billboard |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920235134/https://www.billboard.com/articles/columns/pop/8543407/elton-john-top-male-solo-artist-interview |archive-date=20 September 2020 |access-date=5 February 2020}}</ref> He is the most successful solo artist in the history of the US [[Billboard charts|''Billboard'' charts]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Greatest of All Time Artists |url=https://www.billboard.com/charts/greatest-of-all-time-artists/ |magazine=Billboard |access-date=21 March 2023 |archive-date=28 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528224034/https://www.billboard.com/charts/greatest-of-all-time-artists/ |url-status=live}}</ref> His tribute single to [[Diana, Princess of Wales]], "[[Candle in the Wind 1997]]", a rewritten version of [[Candle in the Wind|his 1974 single]], sold over 33{{nbsp}}million copies worldwide and is the [[List of best-selling singles|best-selling chart single of all time]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Beech |first=Mark |date=28 August 2017 |title=Elton John's Diana Tribute Still Best-Selling Chart Single, 20 Years On |magazine=Forbes |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/markbeech/2017/08/28/diana-tribute-still-biggest-selling-chart-single-20-years-on/|url-status=live|access-date=16 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210716192731/https://www.forbes.com/sites/markbeech/2017/08/28/diana-tribute-still-biggest-selling-chart-single-20-years-on/|archive-date=16 July 2021 |quote=As the world remembers the tragic death of the Princess of Wales 20 years ago, data confirms that a tribute record to her remains the best-selling chart single of all time.}}</ref><ref == Early life and education ==
Reginald Kenneth Dwight was born on 25 March 1947 in [[Pinner]], [[Middlesex]] (now part of the [[London Borough of Harrow]]), the eldest child of Stanley Dwight (1925–1991) and only child of Sheila Eileen (née Harris; 1925–2017), who had married in 1945.<ref name="Telegraph-detective">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/1435132/Family-detective-Elton-John.html |title=Family detective: Elton John |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=24 November 2006<!-- archives disagree with current page --> |access-date=22 July 2025 |last=Barratt |first=Nick |location=London, England |archive-date=11 October 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011165840/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/main.jhtml?xml=%2Fnews%2Fexclusions%2Ffamilyhistory%2Ffheltonjohn.xml |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Sir Elton John 'in shock' after his mother dies aged 92 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-42220913 |access-date=12 November 2018 |work=BBC News |date=4 December 2017 |archive-date=11 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181111180058/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-42220913 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Sir Elton John's father didn't approve of his career path |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/entertainment/news/article.cfm?c_id=1501119&objectid=11542512 |access-date=12 November 2018 |work=The New Zealand Herald |archive-date=13 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181113030241/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/entertainment/news/article.cfm?c_id=1501119&objectid=11542512 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was raised in a [[council house]] in Pinner where his maternal grandparents lived.<ref name="55Pinner" /> When he was six, the family moved to a nearby semi-detached house.<ref name="55Pinner">{{cite web |url=http://www.onthisveryspot.com/spot/Elton_John_Birthplace |title=55 Pinner Hill Road |publisher=On This Very Spot |date=25 March 1947 |access-date=25 February 2009 |archive-date=15 January 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115210301/http://www.onthisveryspot.com/spot/Elton_John_Birthplace |url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref name="Telegraph-detective" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.onthisveryspot.com/spot/111_Potter_Street |title=111 Potter Street |publisher=On This Very Spot |date=15 July 2007 |access-date=25 February 2009 |archive-date=6 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090406053021/http://www.onthisveryspot.com/spot/111_Potter_Street |url-status=usurped}}</ref> He was educated at Pinner Wood Junior School, Reddiford School and [[Pinner County Grammar School]], until he was 17, when he left just before his [[A-Level]] examinations to pursue a career in music.<ref name="Norman">{{cite book |last=Norman |first=Philip |author-link=Philip Norman (author) |date=1991 |title=Elton John |publisher=Fireside |isbn=0-671-79729-8}}</ref><ref name="Rosenthal">Elizabeth Rosenthal, ''His Song: The Musical Journey of Elton John'', Billboard Books, 2001.</ref><ref name="VisualDoc">{{cite book |title=Elton John: The Visual Documentary |first=Nigel |last=Goodall |year=1993 |publisher=[[Omnibus Press]] |isbn=0-7119-3078-3}}</ref>

When John began to consider a career in music seriously, his father, who served in the [[Royal Air Force]], tried to steer him toward a more conventional career, such as banking.<ref>London Gazette, various editions.</ref><ref name="Norman" /> John has said that his wild stage costumes and performances were his way of letting go after a restrictive childhood.<ref name="VisualDoc" /> Both his parents were musically inclined, his father having been a trumpet player with the Bob Millar Band, a semi-professional big band that played at military dances.<ref name="VisualDoc" /> The Dwights were keen record buyers, exposing John to the popular singers and musicians of the day.

John started playing his grandmother's piano as a young boy,<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.npr.org/2018/11/15/668291963/watch-elton-john-get-worse-at-the-piano-in-time-traveling-christmas-ad |title=Tear-Jerker British Ad Re-Creates Elton John's Christmas Past |publisher=NPR|access-date=18 November 2018|archive-date=17 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117082406/https://www.npr.org/2018/11/15/668291963/watch-elton-john-get-worse-at-the-piano-in-time-traveling-christmas-ad|url-status=live}}</ref> and within a year his mother heard him picking out [[Waldteufel]]'s "The [[Skater's Waltz]]" by ear.<ref name="Norman" /><ref name="Rosenthal" /> After performing at parties and family gatherings, at age seven, he began formal piano lessons. He showed musical aptitude at school, including the ability to compose melodies, and gained some notoriety by playing like [[Jerry Lee Lewis]] at school functions. At age 11, he won a junior scholarship to the [[Royal Academy of Music]]. According to one of his instructors, John promptly played back, like a "gramophone record", a four-page piece by [[George Frideric Handel]] after hearing it for the first time.<ref name="Rosenthal" />
[[File:Royal Academy of Music.jpg|thumb|right|Elton John (known then as Reg Dwight) studied at the [[Royal Academy of Music]] in London for five years.]]
For the next five years, John attended Saturday classes at the Academy in central London, and he has said he enjoyed playing [[Frédéric Chopin]] and [[Johann Sebastian Bach]] and singing in the choir during Saturday classes, but that he was not otherwise a diligent classical student.<ref name="Rosenthal" /> "I kind of resented going to the Academy," he said. "I was one of those children who could just about get away without practising and still pass, scrape through the grades."<ref name="Rosenthal" /> He has said that he would sometimes skip classes and ride around on the [[London Underground]].<ref name="Rosenthal" /> Several instructors have attested that he was a "model student", and during the last few years he took lessons from a private tutor in addition to his classes at the Academy.<ref name="Rosenthal" /> He left the Academy before taking the final exams.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/6455921.stm |title=Sixty things for Sir Elton's 60th |work=BBC News |date=23 March 2007 | access-date= 20 September 2019 | archive-date= 6 May 2021 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210506112406/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/6455921.stm | url-status= live}}</ref>

John's mother, though strict with her son, was more outgoing than her husband, and something of a free spirit. With Stanley Dwight uninterested in his son and often absent, John was raised primarily by his mother and maternal grandmother. When his father was home, the Dwights had vehement arguments that greatly distressed John.<ref name="Rosenthal" /> When he was 14, they divorced. His mother then married a local painter, Fred Farebrother, a caring and supportive stepfather whom John affectionately called "Derf" ("Fred" backward).<ref name="Rosenthal" /> They moved into flat No.&nbsp;3A in an eight-unit apartment building called Frome Court, not far from both previous homes. John wrote the songs that launched his career as a rock star, there. He lived there until he had four albums, simultaneously, in the American Top 40.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.shadyoldlady.com/location.php?loc=1617 |title=Elton John Lived Here |publisher=The Shady Old Lady's Guide to London |date=3 April 2007 |access-date=27 July 2020 |archive-date=28 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200728015934/http://www.shadyoldlady.com/location.php?loc=1617 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== 1962–1969: Pub pianist to staff songwriter ===
{{See also|Bluesology}}
At age 15, with his mother's and stepfather's help, John was hired as a pianist at a nearby pub, the Northwood Hills Hotel, playing Thursday to Sunday nights.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qOECAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA76 |title=Music |magazine=Atlanta Magazine |page=76 |access-date=15 January 2016 |date=June 2003 |archive-date=14 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210814032548/https://books.google.com/books?id=qOECAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA76 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.onthisveryspot.com/find/spot.php?spot_web_name=Northwood_Hills_Pub |title=Northwood Hills Pub – On This Very Spot |publisher=onthisveryspot.com |access-date=3 February 2010 |archive-date=26 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626183039/http://www.onthisveryspot.com/find/spot.php?spot_web_name=Northwood_Hills_Pub |url-status=usurped}}</ref> Known simply as "Reggie", he played a range of popular standards, including songs by [[Jim Reeves]] and [[Ray Charles]], as well as his own songs.<ref name="Costello interview">{{cite episode |title=Elton John |url=http://www.sundancechannel.com/films/500328605 |series=Spectacle |series-link=Spectacle: Elvis Costello with... |airdate=2008 |season=1 |number=1 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090428144534/http://www.sundancechannel.com/films/500328605 |archive-date=28 April 2009}}</ref><ref name="p70">{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eJGcZSyBflwC&q=elton+john+rocket+man+elton+john+from+a-z+%22Bell%2C+Thom%22&pg=PA7 |title=Rocket Man: Elton John From A – Z |last1=Bernardin |first1=Claude |last2=Stanton |first2=Tom |publisher=Praeger |year=1996 |isbn=978-0-275-95698-1 |edition=Paperback |pages=70|access-date=30 October 2020|archive-date=16 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816084800/https://books.google.com/books?id=eJGcZSyBflwC&q=elton+john+rocket+man+elton+john+from+a-z+%22Bell%2C+Thom%22&pg=PA7|url-status=live}}</ref> A stint with a short-lived group called the Corvettes rounded out his time.<ref name="Rosenthal" /> Although normal-sighted as a teenager, John began wearing horn-rimmed glasses to imitate [[Buddy Holly]].<ref>Goldrosen, John (1979). The Buddy Holly Story. p. 8. Quick Fox.</ref><ref>[https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/music/rockandjazzmusic/4402149/Why-Buddy-Holly-will-never-fade-away.html "Why Buddy Holly will never fade away"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190205093346/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/culture/music/rockandjazzmusic/4402149/Why-Buddy-Holly-will-never-fade-away.html|date=5 February 2019}}. ''The Telegraph''. Retrieved 3 February 2019.</ref>

In 1962, John and some friends formed a band called [[Bluesology]]. By day, he ran errands for a music publishing company; he divided his nights between solo gigs at a London hotel bar and working with Bluesology. By the mid-1960s, Bluesology was backing touring American [[soul music|soul]] and [[R&B]] musicians such as [[the Isley Brothers]], [[Major Lance]] and [[Patti LaBelle and the Bluebelles]]. In 1966, the band became [[Long John Baldry]]'s supporting band and played 16 times at the [[Marquee Club]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.themarqueeclub.net/long-john-baldry |title=The Marquee Club: Long John Baldry – Biography |publisher=themarqueeclub.net |access-date=25 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100704172041/http://www.themarqueeclub.net/long-john-baldry |archive-date=4 July 2010}}</ref>

[[File:EltonJohnPiano.jpg|thumb|right|The 1910 piano on which John composed his first five albums]]
In 1967, John answered an advertisement in the British music paper ''[[New Musical Express]]'', placed by [[Ray Williams (producer)|Ray Williams]], then the [[A&R]] manager for [[Liberty Records]].<ref name="bilb">{{cite magazine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1wkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA56 |magazine=Billboard |date=4 October 1997 |title=30 Years of Music: Elton John with Bernie Taupin |last=Bessman |first=Jim |access-date=27 September 2014 |archive-date=1 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151101225406/https://books.google.com/books?id=1wkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA56 |url-status=live}}</ref> At their first meeting, Williams gave John an unopened envelope of lyrics written by [[Bernie Taupin]], who had answered the same ad.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VHjxxMJLaQ4 |title=Elton John Takes Stephen Through His Entire Catalogue |language=en |time=3:00 |access-date=31 December 2024 |people=Elton John |work=[[The Late Show with Stephen Colbert]] |archive-date=16 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241216145004/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VHjxxMJLaQ4 |url-status=live }}</ref> John wrote music for the lyrics and then sent it to Taupin, which began their decades-long partnership that {{as of |2012 |alt=still continues}}. When the two first met in 1967, they recorded the first John/Taupin song, "Scarecrow". Six months later, John began going by the name Elton John in homage to two members of Bluesology: saxophonist [[Elton Dean]] and vocalist [[Long John Baldry]].<ref name="Costello interview" /> He legally [[Name change#United Kingdom|changed his name]] to Elton Hercules John on 7 January 1972.<ref>[https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/45571/page/403/data.pdf "Change of Name"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921013533/https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/45571/page/403/data.pdf|date=21 September 2017}}. ''The London Gazette''. Retrieved 28 October 2018.</ref> "Hercules" came from the name of a horse in [[British sitcom]] ''[[Steptoe and Son]]'', of which John was a big fan.<ref>{{cite magazine |date=28 May 2019 |title=Elton John: five things you may not know about the singer |url=https://theweek.com/five-things/101438/five-things-you-didn-t-know-about-elton-john |access-date=12 September 2024 |magazine=The Week |language=en}}</ref>

The team of John and Taupin joined [[Dick James]]'s [[DJM Records]] as staff songwriters in 1968, and over the next two years wrote material for various artists, among them [[Roger Cook (songwriter)|Roger Cook]] and [[Lulu (singer)|Lulu]].<ref name="Vinita">{{Cite book |title=Profiles in Popular Music |last=Vinita |publisher=Sura Books |year=2005 |page=79 |isbn=978-81-7478-638-8}}</ref> Taupin would write a batch of lyrics in under an hour and give it to John, who would write music for each of them in half an hour, disposing of the lyrics if he could not come up with anything quickly.<ref name="Vinita" /> For two years they wrote [[easy-listening]] tunes for James to peddle to singers. Their early output included a contender for the UK entry for the [[Eurovision Song Contest 1969]], for Lulu, called "I Can't Go On (Living Without You)". It [[United Kingdom in the Eurovision Song Contest 1969|came sixth]] of six songs. In 1969, John provided piano for [[Roger Hodgson]] on his first released single, "Mr. Boyd" by Argosy, a quartet that was completed by [[Caleb Quaye]] and [[Nigel Olsson]].<ref>Joynson, Vernon (1995). [http://alextsu.narod.ru/borderlinebooks/uk6070s/index.html ''The Tapestry of Delights''] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111130151831/http://alextsu.narod.ru/borderlinebooks/uk6070s/index.html |date=30 November 2011 }} . London: Borderline Books. See entry on "Argosy".</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Roger Hodgson of Supertramp |url=http://www.ctv.ca/CTVNews/SpecialEvent2/20070608/DianaConcert_Hodgson_070608/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120020509/http://www.ctv.ca/CTVNews/SpecialEvent2/20070608/DianaConcert_Hodgson_070608/ |archive-date=20 January 2012 |access-date=27 September 2014 |publisher=[[CTV News]]}}</ref>

=== 1969–1973: ''Empty Sky'' to ''Goodbye Yellow Brick Road'' ===
[[File:Popzanger Elton John in Nederland Elton John , kop, Bestanddeelnr 924-2765 (cropped).jpg|thumb|275x275px|John in 1971]]
On the advice of music publisher Steve Brown, John and Taupin began writing more complex songs for John to record for DJM. The first was the single "[[I've Been Loving You]]" (1968), produced by [[Caleb Quaye]], Bluesology's former guitarist. In 1969, with Quaye, drummer Roger Pope, and bassist Tony Murray, John recorded another single, "[[Lady Samantha]]", and an album, ''[[Empty Sky]]''. For their follow-up album, ''[[Elton John (album)|Elton John]]'', John and Taupin enlisted [[Gus Dudgeon]] as producer and [[Paul Buckmaster]] as musical arranger. ''Elton John'' was released in April 1970 on DJM Records/[[Pye Records]] in the UK and [[Uni Records]] in the US, and established the formula for subsequent albums: gospel-chorded rockers and poignant ballads. The album's first single, "[[Border Song]]", peaked at 92 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. The second, "[[Your Song]]", reached number seven in the [[UK Singles Chart]] and number eight in the US, becoming John's first hit single as a singer.<ref name="Charts">[http://www.officialcharts.com/artist/_/Elton%20John "Elton John: UK Chart History"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214060116/http://www.officialcharts.com/artist/_/Elton%20John|date=14 February 2015}}. Official Charts Company. Retrieved 3 December 2014.</ref> The album soon became his first hit album, reaching number four on the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]] and number five on the [[UK Albums Chart]].<ref name="Charts" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eJGcZSyBflwC&q=elton+john+rocket+man+elton+john+from+a-z+%22Bell%2C+Thom%22&pg=PA7 |title=Rocket Man: Elton John From A – Z |last1=Bernardin |first1=Claude |last2=Stanton |first2=Tom |publisher=Praeger |year=1996 |isbn=978-0-275-95698-1 |edition=Paperback |pages=116|access-date=30 October 2020|archive-date=16 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816084800/https://books.google.com/books?id=eJGcZSyBflwC&q=elton+john+rocket+man+elton+john+from+a-z+%22Bell%2C+Thom%22&pg=PA7|url-status=live}}</ref>

Backed by former [[Spencer Davis Group]] drummer [[Nigel Olsson]] and bassist [[Dee Murray]], John's first American concert took place at the [[Troubadour (West Hollywood, California)|Troubadour]] in Los Angeles, California on 25 August 1970, and was a success.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eJGcZSyBflwC&q=elton+john+rocket+man+elton+john+from+a-z+%22Bell%2C+Thom%22&pg=PA7 |title=Rocket Man: Elton John From A – Z |last1=Bernardin |first1=Claude |last2=Stanton |first2=Tom |publisher=Praeger |year=1996 |isbn=978-0-275-95698-1 |edition=Paperback |pages=152|access-date=30 October 2020|archive-date=16 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816084800/https://books.google.com/books?id=eJGcZSyBflwC&q=elton+john+rocket+man+elton+john+from+a-z+%22Bell%2C+Thom%22&pg=PA7|url-status=live}}</ref> The concept album ''[[Tumbleweed Connection]]'' was released in October 1970 and reached number two in the UK and number five in the US.<ref name="Charts" /> The live album ''[[17-11-70]]'' (titled ''11–17–70'' in the US) was recorded at a live show aired from A&R Studios on [[WABC-FM]] in New York City. Sales of the live album took a blow in the US when an east-coast [[bootleg recording|bootlegger]] released the performance several weeks before the official album, including all 60 minutes of the aircast, not just the 40 minutes selected by Dick James Music.<ref>{{cite book |last=Heylin |first=Clinton |title=Bootleg: The Secret History of the Other Recording Industry |publisher=St. Martin's Griffin |year=1996 |isbn=0-312-14289-7 |location=New York City |page=66}}</ref>

[[File:Elton John Hamburg 1972 1603720004.jpg|thumb|left|John at the [[Musikhalle Hamburg]], in March 1972]]
John and Taupin wrote the soundtrack to the 1971 film ''[[Friends (1971 film)|Friends]]'' and the album ''[[Madman Across the Water]]'', which reached number eight in the US and included the hit songs "[[Levon (song)|Levon]]" and the album's opening track, "[[Tiny Dancer]]". In 1972, [[Davey Johnstone]] joined the Elton John Band on guitar and backing vocals. Released in 1972, ''[[Honky Château]]'' became John's first US number-one album, spending five weeks at the top of the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]], and began a streak of seven consecutive US number-one albums.<ref>[https://rockhall.com/inductees/elton-john/bio/ "Elton John Biography: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161219054137/https://rockhall.com/inductees/elton-john/bio/|date=19 December 2016}}. Rock Hall. Retrieved 3 December 2014.</ref> The album reached number two in the UK, and spawned the hit singles "[[Rocket Man (song)|Rocket Man]]" and "[[Honky Cat]]".<ref>{{Citation |last=Erlewine |first=Stephen Thomas |title=Honky Château – Elton John {{!}} Album {{!}} AllMusic |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/honky-ch%C3%A2teau-mw0000650320 |access-date=21 April 2024 |language=en |archive-date=22 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922042214/https://www.allmusic.com/album/honky-ch%C3%A2teau-mw0000650320 |url-status=live }}.</ref>

In 1972, John performed at the [[Royal Variety Performance]], where he was upstaged by the dancing of [[Larry Smith (musician)|Larry Smith]], the drummer with the [[Bonzo Dog Doo-Dah Band]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dangerousminds.net/comments/elton_john_upstaged_by_legs_larry_smith_royal_command_performance_1972 |title=Elton John upstaged by 'Legs' Larry Smith: Royal Command Performance 1972 |date=11 September 2012 |website=DangerousMinds|access-date=27 March 2022|archive-date=14 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240614014816/https://dangerousminds.net/comments/elton_john_upstaged_by_legs_larry_smith_royal_command_performance_1972|url-status=live}}</ref> Smith was invited to join John's second US tour; Smith later said: "I suggested adding in various other bizarre elements like me doing "[[Singin' in the Rain (song)|Singin' in the Rain]]" as a song and dance act with Elton playing piano. Kubrick's ''[[A Clockwork Orange (film)|Clockwork Orange]]'' film had recently featured that song. Plus I designed crazy, over-the-top costumes and giant stage sets – known as 'Legstravaganzas'. Elton loved all of it."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pennyblackmusic.co.uk/Home/Details?id=26870 |title='Legs' Larry Smith – Interview 2010 |first=Nick |last=Dent-Robinson |website=pennyblackmusic.co.uk|access-date=27 March 2022|archive-date=8 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220308004426/https://pennyblackmusic.co.uk/Home/Details?id=26870|url-status=live}}</ref>

The pop album ''[[Don't Shoot Me I'm Only the Piano Player]]'' came out at the start of 1973 and reached number one in the UK, the US, and Australia, among other countries.<ref name="Charts" /> The album produced the hits "[[Crocodile Rock]]", his first US ''Billboard'' Hot 100 number&nbsp;one, and "[[Daniel (Elton John song)|Daniel]]", which reached number two in the US and number four in the UK.<ref name="Charts" /><ref>{{cite book |title=Rock N' Roll Gold Rush |url=https://archive.org/details/rocknrollgoldrus00dean |url-access=limited |last=Dean |first=Maury |author-link=Maury Dean |year=2003 |publisher=Algora |isbn=0-87586-207-1 |page=[https://archive.org/details/rocknrollgoldrus00dean/page/n61 46]}}</ref> The album and "Crocodile Rock" were respectively the first album and single on the consolidated [[MCA Records]] label in the US, replacing MCA's other labels, including Uni.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Don't Shoot Me I'm Only The Piano Player |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/albumreviews/dont-shoot-me-im-only-the-piano-player-19730315 |author=Holden, S. |magazine=Rolling Stone |date=15 March 1973 |access-date=12 December 2014 |archive-date=14 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141214215924/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/albumreviews/dont-shoot-me-im-only-the-piano-player-19730315 |url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road]]'', a double-album released in October 1973, gained instant critical acclaim and topped the chart on both sides of the Atlantic, remaining at number one for two months.<ref name="Redbeard GYBR interview">{{cite web |url=http://www.inthestudio.net/ |title=Elton John – Goodbye Yellow Brick Road |last=Redbeard |year=2009 |work=In the Studio With Redbeard, Interviews With Famous Musicians |publisher=Barbarosa Ltd. Production |pages=Studio Interview with Elton John |access-date=13 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140208014251/http://www.inthestudio.net/ |archive-date=8 February 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> It also temporarily established John as a [[glam rock]] star. It contained the US number&nbsp;1 "[[Bennie and the Jets]]", along with the hits "[[Goodbye Yellow Brick Road (song)|Goodbye Yellow Brick Road]]", "[[Candle in the Wind]]", "[[Saturday Night's Alright for Fighting]]" and "[[Funeral for a Friend/Love Lies Bleeding]]".

=== 1974–1980: The Rocket Record Company to ''21 at 33'' ===
[[File:Elton John.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|John on the piano during a live performance in 1975]]
John formed his own record label, [[The Rocket Record Company]] (distributed in the US by MCA and initially by Island in the UK), and signed acts to it—notably [[Neil Sedaka]] (John sang background vocals on Sedaka's "[[Bad Blood (Neil Sedaka song)|Bad Blood]]") and [[Kiki Dee]], in whom he took a personal interest. Rather than releasing his own records through The Rocket Record Company, John signed an $8&nbsp;million contract with MCA Records. Upon the signing of the deal in 1974, MCA reportedly secured a $25&nbsp;million insurance policy on his life.<ref>[https://www.rollingstone.com/music/artists/elton-john/news/artists/8828/56076/56108 Elton John | Rolling Stone Music]{{dead link|date=August 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} 2001 encyclopedia. ''[[Rolling Stone]]''.</ref> In 1974, MCA released ''[[Elton John's Greatest Hits]]'', a UK and US number one that is [[RIAA certification#RIAA Diamond certifications|certified Diamond]] by the [[RIAA]] for US sales of 17{{nbsp}}million copies.<ref name="Charts" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://riaa.com/goldandplatinum.php?content_selector=top-diamond-awards |title=RIAA – Diamond Awards |publisher=Record Industry Association of America |format=PHP |access-date=5 January 2015 |archive-date=20 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720180605/http://riaa.com/goldandplatinum.php?content_selector=top-diamond-awards |url-status=live}}</ref>

In 1974, John collaborated with [[John Lennon]] on his cover of [[the Beatles]]' "[[Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds]]", the B-side of which was Lennon's "One Day at a Time". It was number 1 for two weeks in the US. In return, John was featured on "[[Whatever Gets You Thru the Night]]" on Lennon's album ''[[Walls and Bridges]]''. Later that year, in Lennon's last major live performance, the pair performed these two number-one hits, along with the Beatles' "[[I Saw Her Standing There]]", at [[Madison Square Garden]] in New York City. Lennon made the rare stage appearance with John and his band to keep the promise he had made that he would appear on stage with him if "Whatever Gets You Thru The Night" became a US number-one single.<ref>Jeff Woolf, Scott Jennings and James L. Halperin (Editors) [https://books.google.com/books?id=l-o1rcQ9Cc0C&pg=PA90 Icons of 20th Century Music: Heritage-Odyssey Auction] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161226022135/https://books.google.com/books?id=l-o1rcQ9Cc0C&pg=PA90|date=26 December 2016}} ''Heritage Capital Corporation''.</ref> ''[[Caribou (album)|Caribou]]'' was released in 1974, becoming John's third number one in the UK and topping the charts in the US, Canada and Australia.<ref name="Charts" /><ref name="artists.letssingit.com">{{cite web |url=http://artists.letssingit.com/elton-john-album-caribou-18ftw4 |title=Elton John – Caribou Album |publisher=Artists.letssingit.com |date=17 July 2008 |access-date=6 August 2010 |archive-date=23 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110823192832/http://artists.letssingit.com/elton-john-album-caribou-18ftw4 |url-status=live}}</ref> Reportedly recorded in two weeks between live appearances, it featured "[[The Bitch Is Back]]" and "[[Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me]]".<ref name="artists.letssingit.com" /> "[[Step into Christmas]]" was released as a stand-alone single in November 1973, and appears in the album's 1995 remastered reissue.<ref>Stephen Thomas Erlewine [https://www.allmusic.com/album/release/caribou-bonus-tracks-mr0000283518 "Caribou"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115210716/http://www.allmusic.com/album/release/caribou-bonus-tracks-mr0000283518 |date=15 January 2016}}. AllMusic. Retrieved 10 December 2014.</ref>

{{multiple image
| align  = left
| image1 = Elton john cher show 1975.JPG
| width1 = 150
| image2 = Elton John’s shoes (4) (23219556921).jpg
| width2 = 143
| footer = Influenced by the [[glam rock]] scene in the UK, John (pictured left on the ''[[Cher (TV series)|Cher]]'' show) often wore elaborate stage costumes, including platform boots (right).<ref>P. Auslander, "Watch that man David Bowie: Hammersmith Odeon, London, July 3, 1973" in I. Inglis, ed., ''Performance and Popular Music: History, Place and Time'' (Aldershot: Ashgate, 2006), {{ISBN|0-472-06868-7}}, p. 72.</ref>}}
[[Pete Townshend]] of [[the Who]] asked John to play the "Local Lad" in [[Tommy (1975 film)|the 1975 film adaptation]] of the [[rock opera]] ''[[Tommy (The Who album)|Tommy]]'', and to perform the song "[[Pinball Wizard]]". Drawing on [[power chord]]s, John's version was recorded and used in the movie. The song charted at number&nbsp;7 in the UK.<ref name="Charts" /> John, who had adopted a glam aesthetic on stage, would later state glam rock icon [[Marc Bolan]] "had a great effect on me."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Petridis |first1=Alex |title=Why Marc Bolan was 'the perfect pop star', by Elton John, U2 and more |url=https://www.theguardian.com/music/2020/sep/04/marc-bolan-perfect-pop-star-t-rex-singer-tribute-album-elton-john-u2 |access-date=1 July 2022 |work=The Guardian |date=4 September 2020}}</ref>

The 1975 autobiographical album ''[[Captain Fantastic and the Brown Dirt Cowboy]]'' debuted at number one in the US, the [[Billboard 200#Additional milestones|first album]] to do so, and stayed there for seven weeks.<ref name="record">[https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/61880/elton-expands-captain-fantastic-with-live-tracks "Elton Expands 'Captain Fantastic' With Live Tracks"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161215233658/http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/61880/elton-expands-captain-fantastic-with-live-tracks |date=15 December 2016}}. ''Billboard''. Retrieved 3 December 2014.</ref> John revealed his previously ambiguous personality on the album, with Taupin's lyrics describing their early days as struggling songwriters and musicians in London. The lyrics and accompanying photo booklet are infused with a specific sense of place and time that is otherwise rare in his music. The hit single from this album, "[[Someone Saved My Life Tonight]]", captured an early turning point in John's life. The album's release signalled the end of the Elton John Band, as an unhappy and overworked John dismissed Olsson and Murray.<ref name="Hombach">Jean-Pierre Hombach. "Elton John". pp. 431–439. Lulu.</ref>

According to ''[[Circus (magazine)|Circus]]'', a spokesman for John's manager [[John Reid (music manager)|John Reid]] said the decision was reached mutually via phone while John was in Australia promoting ''Tommy''.<ref name=raves>[[Circus (magazine)|Circus]], No 115, August 1975. Vol 2, No 8. K48002 pp.14–15.</ref> Davey Johnstone and Ray Cooper were retained, Quaye and Roger Pope returned, and the new bassist was Kenny Passarelli; this rhythm section provided a heavier backbeat. [[James Newton Howard]] joined to arrange in the studio and to play keyboards.<ref name="Elton Band" /> In June 1975, John introduced the line-up at the London, England, [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]].<ref name="Elton Band">[http://www.eltonjohn.com/band/james-newton-howard/ "Elton John Band Archives"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306045742/http://www.eltonjohn.com/band/james-newton-howard/ |date=6 March 2016 }}. EltonJohn.com. Retrieved 14 December 2014.</ref>

[[File:Elton John receiving his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|John receiving his star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1975]]
The rock-oriented ''[[Rock of the Westies]]'' entered the US albums chart at number&nbsp;1, as had ''Captain Fantastic and the Brown Dirt Cowboy'', a previously unattained feat.<ref name="record" /> John's stage wardrobe now included ostrich feathers, $5,000 spectacles that spelled his name in lights, and costumes such as the [[Statue of Liberty]], [[Donald Duck]], and [[Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart]].<ref>Nigel Goodall (1993). ''Elton John: a visual documentary'' Omnibus Press, 1993.</ref> In 1975, he received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]].<ref name="HWOF">Jeff Woolf, Scott Jennings and James L. Halperin (2004). "605 Icons of 20th Century Music Autograph Auction Catalog". p. 89. Heritage Capital Corporation.</ref> The album features his fifth US number-one single, "[[Island Girl]]". To celebrate five years since he had first appeared at the venue, in 1975, John played a two-night, four-show stand at [[The Troubadour (Los Angeles)|the Troubadour]]. With seating limited to fewer than 500 attendees per show, tickets were distributed through a postcard lottery system, with each selected individual eligible to purchase two tickets. All attendees received a hardbound "yearbook" documenting the band's history. That year, he also played piano on [[Kevin Ayers]]'s ''[[Sweet Deceiver]]'' and was among the first and few white artists to appear on the African-American television series ''[[Soul Train]]''.<ref name="Redbeard GYBR interview" /> On 9 August 1975, John was named the outstanding rock personality of the year at the first annual Rock Music Awards in Santa Monica, California.<ref>United Press International, "Elton John Named Rock Personality", ''Playground Daily News'', Fort Walton Beach, Florida, 11 August 1975, Vol 30, Number 159, p. 14.</ref> In May 1976, the live album ''[[Here and There (Elton John album)|Here and There]]'' was released, followed in October by the album ''[[Blue Moves]]'', which contained the single "[[Sorry Seems to Be the Hardest Word]]". His biggest success in 1976 was "[[Don't Go Breaking My Heart]]", a duet with Kiki Dee that topped a number of charts, including the UK, the US, Australia, France and Canada.<ref name="Charts" /><ref name="Billboard Charts" />

In addition to being the most commercially successful period of John's career, the years 1970 to 1976 are also widely regarded as his critical peak. Between 1972 and 1975, he achieved seven consecutive number-one albums in the United States, a feat that had not been accomplished prior to that time.<ref name="Redbeard GYBR interview" /> All six of his albums to make ''Rolling Stone''{{'}}s 2003 list of "[[The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time]]" are from this period, with ''Goodbye Yellow Brick Road'' ranked highest at number&nbsp;91.<ref>{{cite book |title=Rolling Stone 500 Greatest Albums of All Time |publisher=Turnaround |year=2006 |isbn=1-932958-61-4 |editor-last=Levy |editor-first=Joe |edition=3rd |location=London, England |language=en |oclc=70672814 |ref=RS500 |editor2-last=Van Zandt |editor2-first=Steven |editor2-link=Steven Van Zandt |orig-year=2005}}</ref> Between 1972 and 1976 he also had six singles reach number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100.<ref name="Billboard charts">{{Cite magazine |url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/elton-john/ |title=Elton John Billboard Chart History |magazine=Billboard|access-date=10 December 2021|archive-date=28 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220728002703/https://www.billboard.com/artist/elton-john/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Elton John 1.jpg|thumb|John performing live in [[Dublin]] with [[Ray Cooper]] in 1979]]
In November 1977, John announced he was retiring from performing; Taupin began collaborating with others.
